The capacitance extraction can be performed without direct electrical contact to the DUT.

articleTitle: A compact CPW-fed monopole antenna for dual-band circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A monopole antenna with coplanar-waveguide (CPW)-feeding structure has been developed in this study for multiple wireless communication system integration. A right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) radiating wave at 1.57 GHz and a left-hand circularly polarized (LHCP) radiating wave at 2.33 GHz are generated for the global positioning system (GPS) and the satellite digital audio radio (SDAR) service system by utilizing bent feeding topology, asymmetric ground plane, and an L-shaped slot etched in the ground plane, The experimental impedance bandwidths range from 1.40 to 2.98 GHz and from 4.48 to 6.27 GHz. The experimental 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths are 80 MHz at 1.57 GHz and 100 MHz at 2.33 GHz.

articleTitle: Harmonics induced by inverters from a photovoltaic plant in the power grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Certain problems related to the quality of the energy delivered by a photovoltaic power plant are addressed. A photovoltaic park with an installed power of 1 MW is presented, along with the equipment used for coupling the photovoltaic cells with the power grid. Certain electrical quantities were recorded (by using a performing data acquisition system) from the inverter that converts the energy from the string boxes into AC energy delivered to the power grid. The waveforms were analyzed with a Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) software algorithm, relying on original programs. The compliance with the standards was checked considering the computed total harmonic distortions of phase voltages and currents. Significant harmonics of order greater than 40 were revealed by the harmonic analysis. Therefore joint measures meant to standardize and respectively to limit the higher order harmonics are compulsory.

articleTitle: An effective EMI-suppression technique for modern wideband common-mode filters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The paper proposes an effective technique to suppress the electromagnetic interference (EMI) radiated from a wideband common-mode filter for modern high-speed digital circuits. This technique is fulfilled by employing the strip-line technology and adding back-cavity structures. By applying this technique, the total power radiated from the demonstrated filter could be reduced more than 40 dB at its common-mode stopband. The procedure for applying the technique is provided step by step. Each forward step makes closer to the goal of total EMI suppression.

articleTitle: A novel inverse method for automatic UAV line patrolling with magnetic sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: As the trunk of the power system, defects of the overhead transmission lines may result in failure of power system operation. Therefore, line patrolling, which means inspection of the transmission lines should be carried out in a regular routine. This article proposes a novel automatic transmission line patrolling method using UAV and magnetic sensors. Geometric relationship and relative position models are proposed to inverse the location and current of the conductor via optimization algorithms. A simulation platform of three-phase AC transmission lines is established and the feasibility of the two models is verified. A parabola fitting method is exploited to simulate the line sag of the transmission system. The inverse result can be used to guide UAV's patrolling around the line. This method makes UAV autonomous patrolling possible, which brings about lower cost, higher efficiency and broad prospect.

articleTitle: EMC aspects of compact wiring for future aircraft
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The installation of wiring in future aircraft will become a big challenge. Available space for wiring will decrease, while the amount of wiring will increase, since more and more aircraft systems will be electronically driven instead of hydraulically. It is proposed to make wiring systems more compact. The aim of this paper is to investigate EMC aspects of this compact wiring by simulations and measurements in a representative part of a smart wing of a future aircraft.

articleTitle: Broadband models of high voltage power transformers and their use in EMC system simulations of high voltage substations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper we present and apply a methodology to create broadband models of power transformers in the frequency range from 9 kHz to 10 MHz. A power transformer of about 300 MVA rated power used at the interface between high voltage stations and AC-power grid is characterized in various operation modes by small signal measurements of the S-parameters. The measurement procedure is shown to provide passive and repeatable measurement data. We find that within the frequency range of interest the operation setting of the transformer like valve voltage or auxiliary power have only a minor impact on the measurements. The measured data is then post-processed to a black-box model describing the transformer as passive linear multiport. This model is then used in EMC system simulations of radiated emissions of full high voltage substations that are connected to the AC-grid by power transformers.

articleTitle: Modeling IC components based on TLP I-V curves and transient responses from SEED perspective
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The behavioral model based on the I-V curve of the transmission line pulse (TLP) test is practical and convenient, which is commonly used in system-efficient ESD design (SEED). However, the model only based on the I-V curve may lead to the neglect of the transient response of the relevant component. This work confirms the issue that is the neglect of the transient response by comparing the TLP test results between the hybrid-triggered and feedback active clamps. The two active clamps have nearly the same TLP I-V curves, which signify that they can be modeled by one behavioral model based only on TLP I-V data, but the TLP transient test results show that they have the different transient responses. Thus the model only extracted by the I-V curve may not be accurate enough. Furthermore, this work proposes the relevant behavioral models for the two active clamps, which take into account the transient responses in addition to TLP I-V curves. Meanwhile, the detailed analysis process is summarized in this work.

articleTitle: Dielectric constant and loss-tangent extraction using near-field technology and phase delay method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the verifications of two extraction methods for the electrical properties (dielectric constant: 8r and loss-tangent: tanδ) are presented. To verify the two extraction methods (Near-Field Technology method and Phase Delay method), a microstrip line is adopted to calculate the wavelength in dielectric for electrical properties comparison. According to the comparison results, both two extraction methods are well-correlated, also the microstrip line simulation with extracted the electrical properties shows good consistence in Insertion Loss and Return Loss with real sample. Finally, the suitability of the two extraction methods is proved for material electric properties.

articleTitle: A pseudo-supervised machine learning approach to broadband LTI macro-modeling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Neural networks have been popularized by their ability to learn complex, non-linear mappings between features and output spaces. They have been used for learning the mapping between geometry and network parameters for various electrical structures such as interconnects. In this work, a novel neural network architecture is applied to black-box identification problems in which poles and residues of a dynamical system are the quantities to be extracted from frequency domain network parameters. Once poles and residues are extracted, time-domain simulation can be performed using well-establish time-domain simulation techniques.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic shielding of IC package with thin absorbing material coating inside in two different configurations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper focuses the application of absorbing material in Integrated Circuits (IC), proposed that IC package coated absorbing material inside can suppress the electromagnetic interference (EMI) in IC chip which caused by the outside complex electromagnetic environment, as well as reducing the electromagnetic radiation caused by chip itself. This proposal is well demonstrated by finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method. Two different configurations of thin absorbing material coating, “Single” and “Double”, are studied in this paper. In the first of simulation, the complex electromagnetic environment is modeled as the Gaussian incident plane wave; in the second, two adjacent pins are chosen as signal port and ground port, to simulate the electromagnetic radiation caused by chip. Finally, to analyze the performance of absorbing material by comparing shielding effectiveness (SE). The analysis process can provide for IC chip electromagnetic compatibility (EMC).

articleTitle: Near-and far-field shielding effectiveness analysis of magnetic materials and their effect on wireless power charger
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: As the multi-radio high-performance mobile devices and ever increasing functional smart-phones converge to a RF coexisting and high-speed digital platforms, the issue involving with electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) or radio frequency interference (RFI) is getting more design challenging for the system integration of mobile platforms. To prevent RFI noise degrading the RF front-end sensitivity and communications performance, electromagnetic shielding material is usually implemented on EMI noisy chips or modules. For the analysis of near-and far-field effective shielding, we utilize the far-field method of AST M D4935 and near-field testing method IEC 61967-6 originally developed for chip level EMI measurement in this study. Since wireless charging provides a number of efficiency, convenience, cost and safety advantages over the traditional charging cable for smartphones and hand-held industrial devices recently, we will also investigate the effect of magnetic material used in wireless charging coil module for further optimum applications.

articleTitle: Floorplanning for 3D-IC with Through-Silicon via co-design using simulated annealing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we will propose a method for floorplanning in three dimensional integrated circuits (3D-IC), considering the impact of Through-Silicon-Via (TSV). In 3D-IC, multiple device layers are vertically stacked and interconnected by excessive amount of TSVs which occupy a lot of silicon area and increase wire length. In this paper, a simulated annealing (SA) multi-objective optimization algorithm is developed for 3D-IC including the factors of floorplanning, plan functional block and TSV simultaneously. By using this SA method, we can get a floorplanning with minimum TSVs, thus reduces the silicon area and wire length.

articleTitle: Design of balanced wideband filtering circularly polarized antenna using quasi-self-complementary structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a balanced wideband filtering circularly polarized (CP) antenna designed using rectangular quasi-self-complementary structure is proposed. The antenna is fed by a differential microstrip line, and consists of a strip-loaded rectangular slot radiator and its complementary slot-loaded patch counterpart. The fields radiated by the two complementary parts of the antenna are expected to be orthogonal if properly excited. To achieve a CP radiation pattern, a 90° delay line section is embedded in one of the two feedlines to provide 90° phase difference between signals fed to the two antenna input ports. In addition, to suppress the wideband common-mode signals, two half-wavelength microstrip line sections that share part of their structures are connected between the two feedlines for producing two transmission zeros in the DM passband under CM operation. For the designed balanced wideband filtering CP antenna, measurement shows that the |S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dd</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|≤ -10 dB DM operating band covers a frequency range of 3.16-4.63 GHz. Very good CM suppression was observed with the measured CM reflection coefficient greater than -1 dB over most of the DM passband. The simulated 3-dB axial ratio band is 3.04-5.09 GHz.

articleTitle: LMA observation of upward flashes at Säntis Tower: Preliminary results
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Lightning striking tall towers is mainly of the upward lightning type, which is characterized by the absence of a first return stroke and the presence of an initial continuous current (ICC) with or without superimposed pulses. The Säntis Tower is 124 m tall and it is located on the top of the Säntis Mountain (2502 m ASL) in the eastern Swiss Alps. The Tower location exhibited the highest lightning flash density in Switzerland during the period from 1999 to 2006. The Tower was instrumented in May 2010 for the measurement of lightning current parameters. In order to complement these data, a Lightning Mapping Array (LMA) was deployed around the Tower during the Summer 2017. The LMA system locates the sources of radio emissions in the very high frequency range (VHF, 60-66 MHz) in three dimensions by a time-of-arrival analysis. The LMA system allows detailed analysis of individual flashes, through the mapping of the lightning channels in the cloud with sufficient time resolution and spatial precision to locate the origin and propagation of each flash. With the help of the LMA, we intend to further investigate the initiation and propagation characteristics of upward lightning emerging from the Tower. From June 29 to August 15, 2017, 33 upward flashes initiated from the Säntis tower were registered by the LMA network. These records are the first set of VHF total lightning mapping obtained in Switzerland. Preliminary results of the campaign are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Exploration of characteristic mode theory for electromagnetic compatibility modeling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) applications of characteristic mode (CM) analysis will be explored. In particular, two potential EMC applications by CM analysis will be demonstrated. In the first EMC application, the crosstalk between two patch radiators will be evaluated without the information of the excitation source location. The effect of distance between two coupled radiators on the coupling will be demonstrated with the characteristic current distribution. The effect of a conducing wall placed between two coupled radiators will also be evaluated. In the second EMC application, the frequency shift when a patch radiator is placed in an environment with conducting objects will be evaluated. The frequency shift when a patch radiator is placed nearby a conducing wall will be evaluated by the change of resonant frequency in the CM modal significance.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis and circuit modeling of pulsed current injection in wire pairs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Pulsed current injection (PCI) allows testing the immunity of electric/electronics devices against fast and intense transient electromagnetic disturbances. This technique resorts to inductive couplers to directly inject noise currents into the harness entering the device under test (DUT). Although the characteristics of the stress waveform to be induced at the DUT input are assigned by the Standards, and set by calibration, the noise actually entering the DUT input ports may exhibit significant differences due to the frequency response of the injection device itself as well as specific setup arrangements. To investigate these influence factors, possibly compromising test significance, in this work a PCI test setup involving a wire-pair is setup and modeled in the SPICE environment. Measurements and simulations are exploited to put in evidence the effects that the presence of other wires (and their terminations) in the bundle play on the voltage waveform induced at the terminations of a specific wire. The results here presents are significant also in view of extending the analysis to more complex wiring configurations (currently ongoing), and in order to correlate the PCI technique with radiative immunity procedures foreseen by the Standards.

articleTitle: Behaviour of surge protective devices under lightning ground potential rise: Findings from a desk-top study
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Specific points in IEEE Standard 1692 suggested that surge protective devices may not adequately protect equipment under conditions of lightning ground potential rise (GPR). With no further information from the standard, this behavior of a particular surge protective device (SPD) was investigated by means of a desk-top study. As reference signatures, common mode and differential mode waveforms presented by the SPD, with full complement of components and when individual components were removed from the SPD, were captured under impulse conditions without emulated lightning GPR. The SPD was then applied in the test set-up with emulated lightning GPR. The study clearly showed the importance of correctly bonding components downstream of the SPD. When not correctly bonded, the SPD behaved as if the transient voltage suppressor diode of the SPD was not present that led to expected downstream equipment damage.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic wave in automotive cabin using complex Poynting's theorem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Due to the fast spread of the electric cars and the advanced driver assistance systems in recent years, it is necessary to reduce the electromagnetic noise from the power electronics, which are usually in high speed and with large electricity, and in the meantime to improve the immunity performances of sensing apparatus and communication equipment. The electromagnetic environmental compatibility in the cars will be of more importance in future. In this work, the behavior of electromagnetic waves generated in automotive cabin was estimated by a use of simulation techniques for the case where electromagnetic waves were irradiated into the simple cabin from outside, and we propose a new method to analyze electromagnetic waves propagating in automotive cabin by using Poynting's theorem.

articleTitle: Field uniformity improvement at lower frequencies in a reverberation chamber using metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The field uniformity in most reverberation chambers (RC) generally cannot meet the standards of IEC61000-4-21 in the frequency range between 80 MHz and 200 MHz, which is lower than the lowest usable frequency (LUF) of the RCs. In this paper, we demonstrate that by coating the RCs walls with judiciously designed metasurfaces the field uniformity in the RCs between 80 MHz and 200 MHz can be effectively improved. Actually, the reflective metasurfaces can be designed to tune the phase of scattering waves from the walls and increase the mode numbers in the RCs, thus improving the field uniformity and generating statistically homogeneous, isotropic, incoherent and random fields. Simulation results validate our idea.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modeling of high voltage multi-level converter substations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an electromagnetic simulation methodology and workflow for high voltage multi-level converter stations is presented, which is based on the transmission line matrix method as used in CST Studio Suite. The methodology makes use of the thin wire models of CST, which are well suited to represent the high voltage bus bars and cables connecting the 3-dimensional structures of the converter valves and halls. Additional key components such as grid transformers and phase reactors are included as hybrid models, consisting of 3-dimensional structures in combination with imported circuit netlists. The converter itself is modeled as impulse sources in the CST circuit schematic, where the switching pulse patterns and the cell switching characteristics are taken into account in a final post-processing step in combination with electromagnetic interference (EMI) detector models. The obtained accuracy in the target frequency range from 10 kHz to 10 MHz, is about ±5 dB, when compared to actual electromagnetic (EM) field measurements.

articleTitle: A study on design of differential-paired lines with meander delay line by preference set-based design method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In the design of electric and electronic devices, it is required to pursue a solution which satisfies simultaneously multi-objective performances sometimes including conflicting requirements. This paper newly attempts to propose a concurrent design method in electrical and electronic engineering by applying a multi-objective satisfactory design method, Preference Set-Based Design (PSD), to differential-paired lines with meander delay line. The meander delay line for the equi-length routing are designed using PSD. The design parameters satisfying required performances are obtained in ranges successfully. The validity of the design parameters is demonstrated by numerical modeling. It was demonstrated that PSD is applicable for multi-objective design under the uncertainty problems.

articleTitle: A novel BG-triggered ggNMOS structure for FD-SOI ESD protection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A back-gate-triggered (BG-Triggered) grounded-gate NMOS (ggNMOS) electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection structure is presented for the advanced full-depleted silicon-on-isolation (FD-SOI) process. The proposed device can further reduce the trigger voltage of the typical ggNMOS to meet ESD requirements of the digital core transistors and various pins. This new configuration is characterized by the resistance used to connect the drain and back gate, which can be adjusted to change the electron density and space charge distribution in the channel during an ESD event. Compared with the previous approaches, the proposed ggNMOS is able to achieve an adjustable trigger voltage without extra design complexity and limitations.

articleTitle: Information leakage and recovery from multiple LCDs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Unintentional electromagnetic waves leak out from a liquid crystal display (LCD) monitor, which is the main output device of a computer. When the leaked signal is recovered, the display information of target monitor can be interpreted. Because leakage electromagnetic waves which include video signal information occur in the hardware system after the video signal processor of the LCD monitor radiation band is dependent on the clock frequency. In this paper, a method to distinguish the leaked information from two target monitors which have different refresh rate is proposed.

articleTitle: Quantification of EMI for power-ground plane and novel EBG structure for SSN suppression
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) method and the field equivalence principle are coupled by edge node voltage to quantify the radiation emission of a power/ground plane pair in this paper. Simulation results using the proposed method show a good agreement with the measurement. Meanwhile, in order to suppress the propagation of simultaneous switching noise (SSN) that leads to radiation in packaging, a novel electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure is proposed in this paper and it can achieve ultrawideband suppression of SSN.

articleTitle: Modularized prototype of 5G mmWave base station system at 38 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a 4-way modularized prototype millimeter-wave base station system operating at 38 GHz. The base station contains several separated modules operating for different functions in IF frequency and RF frequency. A 4×4 phased array antenna is utilized in the system for beam-steering or beamforming applications in the future 5G technologies. The whole system is fabricated by standard industrial printed circuit board (PCB) process with Rogers RO4350B material and manufactured circuit components. Measurements of the phased array antenna and the prototype system were done to verify the design concept. The measurement result of the 1-way system has a −28 dB EVM with 600 MHz bandwidth in a 6-meter wireless link scenario.

articleTitle: An ambient energy harvester using metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A 4×4 complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR) array based on metasurface for ambient electromagnetic energy harvesting is designed. We present a feed network to transfer the maximum energy collected by all the array units to a load. Simulations show that the CSRR array can be highly efficient in delivering the maximum received power to one load using the feed network, 99.4% efficiency is achieved at 5.16 GHz. In addition, a rectifier circuit is designed to convert RF energy collected by the array into available DC energy 35.1% conversion efficiency is achieved at −10 dB input power.

articleTitle: Wireless power transfer system for unmanned vehicle using T-shape ferrite structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The missiles and other unmanned vehicles play an important role in the modern and future society. Conventional unmanned vehicles are adopting wired battery charging system. However, in general, unmanned vehicles have a long charging time and short operating time, which is a great obstacle to the utilization of unmanned vehicles. In this paper, a wireless power transfer system using T-shape ferrite is applied to unmanned vehicle. We designed a wireless power transfer system with T-shape ferrite through simulation and verified it through experiments.

articleTitle: Experimental study of the properties of metamaterials using broadside-coupled split ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: We investigated the transmission coefficient, reflection coefficient, and absorbing property of metamaterials using a two-dimensional array of broadside-coupled split ring resonators (BC-SRRs) in free space measurement systems. The resonant frequency is dependent on the dielectric substrate thickness, and the BC-SRRs absorbed electromagnetic waves when a metal plate was placed on the back surface of the sample. Although the derived relative permittivity showed a negative imaginary part in some frequency regions, the correctness can be confirmed from the physical point of view by conversion to the characteristic impedance and the propagation coefficient. The unit cell size of the BC-SRR can be miniaturized to be near 1/14 compared to the free space wavelength.

articleTitle: EM security analysis of compact ECDSA hardware
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents an EM analysis for extracting a signature generation key from ECDSA hardware. In particular, we show a possibility of a horizontal side-channel attack using EM waves radiated from compact ECDSA hardware based on Jacobian projective coordinates. We also mention a possible countermeasure against the attack.

articleTitle: Metalens in microwave region for the generation of orbital angular momentum
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, transmission-type metalenses are proposed to generate vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum in microwave region. By designing and arranging artificial meta-atoms generating phase discontinuities, the vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum with specific topological charge can be obtained by manipulation of local phase. Both simulations and measurements are presented to verify the theoretical approach.

articleTitle: Investigation on the terminal response of a twisted-wire pair excited by EMP
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: It is great harmful that high-power electromagnetic pulse (EMP) enviromment coupling into the electronic instrumentation and system through the different cables and slots. Electromagnetism defense of electronic system should be brought to the radio forefront. So paying attention to coupling characteristic of the twisted wire pair (TWP) excited by high-power EMP in the equipment and system is very necessary. In this paper, we built the field-cable coupling model of the a single twisted-wire pair excited by high-power EMP for the obtain the time-domain termianl response of the twisted wire pair (TWP). The interference coupling response of the twist wire pair with the case that the incident wave is EMP is computed by using an efficient procedure based on the transmission line model (TLM), which involves Thevenin equivalent representation, and the closed-form analytic approximations of the terminal response valid for an arbitrary direction of incidence and polarization of the incoming plane-wave field, and different positions are provided in the frequency. And the transient waveforms for plane-wave field excitations by an inverse discrete Fourier transformation.

articleTitle: Wafer level heterogeneous integration of a millimeter-wave transceiver module and its EMC problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presented the design methodology of 3 dimensional wafer level integrations of packaged transceiver. Low noise, power amplifier, two mixers, packaged oscillator, 1/4 quarter mode SIW filter as well as couplers were designed by using wafer level heterogeneous integrations. The noise figure of the transceiver is about 4 dB with its gain 23dB at 30GHz, the output power is about 2 W. The packaged oscillator can be designed with its packaged low noise amplifier without shielding.

articleTitle: Improving performance of shipboard HF communication antennas by antenna placement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The aim of this study is to improve the operational performance of high frequency (HF) communication antennas mounted on a warship by arranging placements of these antennas. Towards this aim, electromagnetic analysis of HF communication antennas mounted on a warship is performed by using transient solver of Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio® (MWS), in order to determine the optimal locations of these antennas for the operational performance of these antennas to be optimum in terms of electromagnetic coupling and far field radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Impedance calculation of grid power distribution network with irregular shapes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient method is proposed to calculate the impedance of the grid power distribution network (PDN) with irregular shapes. Based on the analysis of the equivalent circuits of grid unit cell and plane unit cell, the irregular shaped grid PDN is simplified to a plane PDN with the same shape. The differences in the grid PDN and equivalent plane PDN are the material parameters of substrate and metal. The equivalent plane PDN has the equivalent conductivity, permeability, relative permittivity and loss tangent. Then, the equivalent plane PDN is efficiently calculated by the finite element method due to its simplified structure. The proposed method can be used to calculate the irregular shaped grid PDN of different sizes. An example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: WLAN MIMO antennas for smart watch applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a MIMO antenna design with for smart watch applications that works in the WLAN bands (2.4/5.2/5.8GHz bands) is proposed. The overall dimensions of the MIMO antenna design are 41×41×4.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and the two-antenna array (including the surrounding housing) are built on FR4 substrate with 0.8 mm thickness and relative permittivity of 4.4. Each antenna array element is a loop antenna type incorporated with a shorted arm. In order to achieve desirable dual-band WLAN operation, an inductor chip is connected in series with the shorting arm that connected to the system ground. Because the proposed MIMO antenna design is small in size and has exhibited good performances and isolation, it is therefore suitable for integrating into any smart watch devices.

articleTitle: Research on EMI control techniques of airborne power electronic equipment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In the process of high-efficiency control of aircraft, power electronic equipment brings a series of electromagnetic interference problems due to its own electromagnetic characteristics, which makes the electromagnetic environment on the aircraft carrier become worse. Therefore, it must take measures to control the electromagnetic interference. In this paper, the mechanism of electromagnetic interference generation of airborne power electronic equipment is analyzed. And some electromagnetic interference control techniques are proposed from the aspects of anti-interference design and electromagnetic compatibility test which can provide technical guidance for electromagnetic compatibility design and testing of airborne power electronic equipment.

articleTitle: Prediction of radiated emission pattern for the device under test
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Procedure to predict the radiated emission pattern in a complex test setup is illustrated in this paper. Device under test (DUT) is divided into three domains to facilitate the electromagnetic simulations. Huygens surface is used to capture the near fields for each domain and then formed single Huygens surface for the given DUT. Near field to far field transformation is applied on this surface to obtain the radiated emission pattern. Radiation from DUT is also captured in terms of total radiated power (TRP) using the radiated emission patterns.

articleTitle: Simplification technique for modeling electromagnetic radiation of shielding cable bundle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Conventional modeling approaches are inefficient for the analysis of electromagnetic radiation problem of shielding cable bundle. Thus, this paper aims at simplifying the modeling of electromagnetic radiation from braided shielding cable bundle. By grouping together the conductors, the complexity of modeling the complete cable bundle is significantly simplified with good accuracy, and the required computation time is markedly reduced over a large frequency range. A constructed model of braided shielding 17-conductor performed on a commercial software CST is illustrated to validate the efficiency and advantages of the presented method.

articleTitle: Time domain FEM computational approach for calibration of surface scan method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The surface scan method constitutes an effective methodology to characterize printed circuit boards and integrated circuits in terms of electromagnetic emission and immunity. It is a useful technique to locate areas of critical radiation or susceptibility which could influence the performance of devices nearby or the device under test itself. The radiated near-field gathered during the test sequence is effectively influenced by the electric-and magnetic-field probes used in the course of the measurement process hence a calibration of the setup is required. This calibration is done via a 3D-FEM-wave simulation in the time domain, stimulated with a Gaussian pulse, to gather the near-field behavior over the frequency range of interest. The numerically derived results can be used during post processing to eliminate the probe's influence on the measured results.

articleTitle: Enabling the next generation USB 3.1 (Gen 2) in mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Optimization methodology of USB 3.1 Gen 1 serial link interface on mobile devices is proposed. The goal is upgrading to USB 3.1 Gen 2 which is running at 10 GB/s. Rigorous 3D electromagnetic full-wave modeling based on a divide and conquer approach is used to analyze both channel loss budget and eye diagrams. Effective driver equalization, interconnect loss and eye opening are the metrics used to optimize the link by means of Design of Experiments and a Response Surface Model. Main factors affecting the time budget of the link are cable's length and on board discontinuities.

articleTitle: Analysis of the relationship between arc power and radiated electromagnetic noise
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: We hypothesize that when the arc power is low, the arc current fluctuates sharply, generating a large amount of radiated electromagnetic noise. To verify our hypothesis, in this study, we analyze the correlation between arc power and high frequency current, and the correlation between arc power and radiated high frequency electromagnetic noise. Our results show that the lower the arc power, the greater the magnitude of the high frequency current and the greater the amount of radiated electromagnetic noise generated, validating our original hypothesis.

articleTitle: 1:4 Tree microstrip interconnect Kron-Branin model
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: An uncommon computational model of printed circuit board (PCB) interconnect tree is developed. The proposed model is based on the Kron-Branin (KB) formalism. This uncommon KB method consists in traducing the tree interconnect network into a graph structure. The graph topology is constituted by the branches, nodes and coupling cords. The mathematical abstraction of the graph enables to establish the KB characteristic of the problem represented by the tree interconnect system. After the branch current calculations, the S-parameter model is established. The uncommon KB model is validated with a prototype of single-input and four-outputs (1:4) microstrip interconnect tree. As expected, the calculated S-parameters from the KB model are in good agreement with simulations and measurements from DC to 4 GHz. Thanks to the computation speed and accuracy, the KB model is prominent for the fast computation of interconnect structures and useful for the PCB EMC and signal integrity analyses.

articleTitle: EMI risk analysis via dedicated evaluation of the susceptibility of medical devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the Electro-Magnetic Interference Risk Analysis of medical devices via the evaluation of their susceptibility. Medical devices for supporting patients' life are frequently applied in vulnerable environments such as hospitals and surgery rooms. The susceptibility analysis is based on a GTEM testing method derived from ANSI C63.18 and is applied to three different medical devices, namely ECG, patient monitor and an infusion pump. Specific interference signals are generated simulating telecommunication devices, more specifically Wi-Fi, GSM, and PMR. The results showed that especially the signals transmitted by the PMR may affect the performance of medical devices.

articleTitle: Multiple OAM modes generated by patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a circular patch antenna, which can generate orbital angular momentum (OAM) radio waves at 2.4GHz, is proposed. The designed model is established with 8 ports for single OAM mode. The OAM vortex waves can be generated by feeding networks with fixed phase delay feeding sources. Furthermore, the proposed antenna can also be used for producing more OAM modes. Multiple OAM modes are generated by multiple feeding networks, which are designed by microstrip lines. Simulation results of phase distribution demonstrate the proposed antenna can actually generate single OAM mode and multiple OAM modes. The transmission coefficient between different OAM modes proves the proposed antenna can be used for wireless communication.

articleTitle: A compact antenna for UWB indoor positioning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this work, a compact antenna which can be used for Ultra-Wide-Band (UWB) indoor localization is designed and simulated. Its performances are analyzed.

articleTitle: Research on sparse adaptive beam-forming based on non-uniform norm for failure elements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an Non-Uniform Norm constrained least mean square (NU-CNLMS) adaptive beam-forming algorithm which can improve the pattern for antenna array with failure elements by exploiting the sparsity property of it. The new algorithm modifies the cost function of classical constrained least mean squares algorithm in order to reach the optimum norm constraint for adaptive beam-forming system with different sparsity. So, we make a great trade-off between the sparsity and estimation bias generated by norm constraint. When employing this algorithm to antenna array, we can get a large aperture antenna array with few elements which is identical to the situation of failure elements existing. We investigate the effectiveness of new algorithm by simulation results which showed the performance of NU-CNLMS is superior to the other sparse adaptive beam-forming in terms of convergence speed and sparsity.

articleTitle: Microwave orbital angular momentum mode multiplexing using circular slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a space-saving and cost-efficient slot antenna system, which can generate l=+1 and l=-1 OAM waves simultaneously at 2.4 GHz, is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the multiplexing antenna system can generate dual-mode OAM waves. Isolation coefficients between different OAM modes achieve -16dB, which provides a better approach for exploiting OAM waves in wireless communication field.

articleTitle: An improved expression of via barrel-plate capacitance based on a convergence study
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: An improved expression of the via barrel-plate capacitance is proposed, based on a thorough convergence study, to solve issues arising from truncating the infinite summation of the original formula. The improved expression demonstrates faster convergence thus requires less effort in summation.

articleTitle: About the immunity of the equipment used to monitor the units of power transformers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The paper deals with problems related to electromagnetic compatibility occurring at an equipment used to monitor and diagnosis units for electric power transformation. Applying numerical methods during the process for data acquisition and processing results into an accurate monitoring, but new aspects had to be considered. They are related to immunity to electromagnetic disturbances. The above mentioned equipment is presented, paying a special attention to the places where problems related to electromagnetic susceptibility can occur: the supplying source, input/output interferences, electronics incorporated in the equipment, data communication systems. The operating modalities of the equipment under test are presented along with the criteria to be accomplished by the equipment. The accomplished immunity tests (performed according to the standards in force) are described and analyzed. They address the electrostatic discharges, the immunity to radiated radio-frequency electromagnetic field, the surge immunity and respectively the power frequency magnetic field immunity after the applying of anti-perturbative measures.

articleTitle: Influence of test table materials on radiated immunity test: Report on investigation using a giant anechoic chamber
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: It has been pointed out for a long time that test table materials greatly influence EMC testing. Although there are several studies on radiated emissions testing, there have been no reports on radiated immunity testing. Therefore, it was verified whether test table materials had influence on electric field strength in testing.

articleTitle: Non-contact monitoring method for overvoltage based on Pockels effect
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: To measure the overvoltage accurately, a non-contact monitoring method based on Pockels effect is proposed. Firstly, the stray capacitance between the energized conductor and the transducer is calculated and connected in series with the dividing capacitor of the transducer in order to constitute a capacitive voltage divider, which can convert the high-amplitude over-voltage signal into a low voltage signal. Secondly, adopt the Pockels electro-optic crystal (Bismuth Germanium Oxide, BGO) with the design of dual-light-channel compensation to measure the low voltage signal, then the value of the high-amplitude overvoltage can be calculated. The feasibility and effectiveness of this method are verified by comparing with the contact measurement.

articleTitle: Plasmonic enhanced emission from nanostructed embedded InGaN/GaN MQWs with silver nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Recently there has been extensive research to address the shortcomings of the widely used phosphor coated Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) such as the slow recombination rate. In-situ Indium rich InGaN quantum dots (QD) was incorporated into multi-quantum wells (MQWs) to generate a broad emission spectrum. In this research, we aim to study the effect of surface plasmon coupling on QD emission by depositing a layer of Silver (Ag) Nanoparticles onto a surface of such MQWs sample. Ag nanoparticles has been shown to be effect in tuning the different intensity and response of these quantum dots incorporated MQWs sample.

articleTitle: Risk assessment and mitigation for the hazards of electromagnetic radiation to fuel during high intensity radiated field testing of aircraft
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: High Intensity Radiated Field (HIRF) testing of, in, and around, aircraft, and aircraft subsystems, that contain fuel (or other potentially explosive atmosphere creating substances) pose particular hazards for Radio Frequency (RF) Induced ignition - Hazards of Electromagnetic Radiation to Fuel (HERF). The primary threat is considered to be from ignition by RF induced sparking/arcing, as this requires far less energy than direct heating effects. Accepted international guidance that is used is contained in “CENELEC CLC/TR 50427: Assessment of Inadvertent Ignition of Flammable Atmospheres by Radio-Frequency Radiation” to identify risks posed by the testing. Where hazardous levels of RF energy are identified as being used within a HIRF test, various mitigations can be used to reduce the overall risk, such as: Air frame/fuel-system review and/or inspection to reduce the probability of any dormant or undetected make/break arcing mechanisms within the flammable atmosphere/ullage; read-across of Electrostatic Discharge (ESD)/Lightning Strike design protection measures that would make the risk non-credible; specifying a minimum fuel load so arcing mechanisms are not in ullage space; use of alternate fuels to change the fuel/air mixture in the ullage to being too rich or too lean; injection of inert atmospheres into the ullage to prevent ignition; identification of alternate assessment strategies and/or potential restriction on HIRF test levels, to identify safe and cost effective assessment solutions for aircraft HIRF clearance activities.

articleTitle: An optimized GPU accelerated pre-conditioned biconjugate gradient stabilized method to speedup the scalar potential finite-difference method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: To improve the efficiency for solving the distribution of the induced electric field in human head during transcranial magnetic stimulation. A GPU accelerated incomplete LU factorization preconditioned biconjugate gradients stabilized method is used to solve the linear equations. A block method is also selected to further increase the calculation speed. The results indicate that the method proposed in this study is much more efficiency which compared to the some existed linear algebra subroutines.

articleTitle: Rapid electro-thermal modeling for 3D integration using circuit simulation techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Device-level electro-thermal analysis is studied using circuit simulation schemes with linear computational complexity. Two methods are explored and tested on a MOSFET. Results are compared with a commercial simulator.

articleTitle: Analytical description of contacting concepts for shielding enclosures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper deals with the analytical description of contacting concepts for shielding enclosures. On material level starts the analysis based on electrical circuit diagrams. After that, an approach is presented for the calculation of parasitic capacitances and coupling inductances to calculate the overall impedance of a test enclosure. Finally, the analytical calculation is compared with a numerical solution and an impedance measurement.

articleTitle: FDTD computation of lightning currents in a multilayer CFRP panel with a conductivity matrix approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The transient distribution of lightning current, which flows in a multilayer carbon-fiber-reinforced plastic (CFRP) material of aircraft, has been studied using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. Each layer of the multilayer CFRP panel has a fiber direction of 45°, 90°, -45° or 0°, and, therefore, has an anisotropic conductivity. It is quite difficult to represent such an anisotropic layered panel using the FDTD method with common rectangular prism or cubic cells. In this paper, the distribution of lightning currents on a 3-mm-thick multilayer CFRP panel, composed of 16 layers, is computed using the FDTD method with a conductivity matrix approach.

articleTitle: The VLF field generated by a loop antenna in the ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Very Low Frequency (VLF: 3-30 kHz) electromagnetic waves are widely used in submarine communications. By so far, the complete expressions of the electromagnetic field generated by a magnetic dipole in arbitrary direction in the F2-layer of the ionosphere have not been given. In this paper, with the dipole source placed in the ionosphere, we will attempt to derive the formulas of the VLF/ELF electromagnetic field on the sea surface. Finally, some new numerical results are obtained and some discussions are also carried out.

articleTitle: Decision rules for metrological confirmation of EMC measurement equipment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In the forthcoming edition of the standard ISO/IEC 17025 emphasis is placed on the “decision rules” according to which conformity to a specified requirement is stated taking measurement uncertainty into account. Decision rules shall be defined in particular for metrological confirmation, i.e. to confirm that a measuring instrument is adequate to its intended use. The level of risk associated with false acceptance and false rejection and inherent with the adopted decision rule shall be calculated. In this work three decision rules are proposed that apply to the case where: a) calibration uncertainty is comparable with the tolerance set by standards, as frequently occurs in the case of electromagnetic compatibility measuring equipment; b) the specification to be met is expressed in terms of a coverage interval corresponding to a given coverage probability; c) no specification or requirement is available and confirmation has to be obtained by comparison with previous calibration data. The three decision rules proposed here are not, and cannot be, exhaustive. Further investigation is underway.

articleTitle: Inductor modeling with Huygens's equivalent model to estimate coupling noise
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Inductors are widely used in PCB electronic systems and often act as radiators to other analog components, while are difficult to do pre-simulation to predict the coupling as the actual physical model of inductors are unavailable for commercial confidentiality. This study is to reconstruct the inductor with Huygens's equivalent model to estimate the near-field coupling in analog circuit design. The transmission scattering parameter S21 of 1 nH to micro-strip line, 3.3 uH to micro-strip line and 3.3 uH to a WIFI antenna totally three cases are calculated to validate the equivalent method. 6 dB discrepancies are observed within the frequency span compared with test result and Huygens's equivalent model simulation. The feasibility provides a possible approach to estimate the whole channel isolation including the inductors, such as coupling from transmitting impedance matching channel to receiving impedance matching channel, buck converter to antenna, etc.

articleTitle: Modeling and measurement of a common-mode filter based on the 3-D transmission line structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel common-mode filter (CMF), based on the 3-D transmission line structure, is proposed for 3-D IC applications. Using the quarter-wavelength resonator, the proposed CMF can suppress the common-mode (CM) noise with little influence on the differential-mode (DM) signal. The results of the full-wave simulations and the measurements are presented and they show a good agreement.

articleTitle: Numerical approach to study layout influence on electromagnetic emissions signature
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Several elements have significant influence on the conducted disturbances of power electronic circuits, such as parasitic elements of the printed board layout and active and passive components. This paper treats the impact of a DC-DC buck converter layout on the Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). Two different routing designs for a chopper circuit are presented. A numerical modelling method is proposed to extract the equivalent circuit for each routing. Using the ANSYS Q3D extractor, based on the combination of the Moment method (MoM) and the finite-element methods (FEMs), the R, L, C matrices are computed for different frequencies. The obtained equivalent models, taking into account all the stray elements, are implemented on Simplorer. Indeed, the complete circuit, designed on this time domain simulator, is constituted by the equivalent circuit layout, the Line Impedance Stabilization Network (LISN) module, and the equivalent electrical model of the passive and active components. Afterwards, conducted disturbances were analytically identified. To validate the simulation results, experiments were performed. A comparative study is carried out in order to quantify the impact of the routing on the EM compatibility signature. A good agreement is obtained.

articleTitle: High efficiency wireless power transfer system robust against misalignment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The power transfer efficiency of magnetic resonance coupling wireless power transfer (WPT) system is sensitive to the alignment of the transmitter and receiver. In this paper, a multi-coil WPT structure is proposed to enhance power transfer efficiency. It is shown by experimental results that the proposed WPT system can achieve 90.2% efficiency in aligned working conditions. Meanwhile, this WPT system maintains over 70% efficiency from 0 to 55 mm misalignment distance, which is 66% of the length of the Rx board. The proposed WPT system is suitable for the applications of implant devices for biomedical health care and treatment.

articleTitle: Problems with stirred immunity measurements in a reverberation chamber: Corrections to DO-160G section 20.6
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: When DO-160G, Environmental Conditions and Test Procedures for Airborne Equipment [1], Section 20.6, was modified in 2010 to simplify electromagnetic susceptibility measurements in a reverberation chamber and switch from a stepped paddle (mode-stepped or mode-tuned) to a continuously moving paddle (mode-stirred), an error was introduced which overestimates the test level by approximately 1.4 to 3 dB, and possibly more (the error should increase with exposure frequency). We offer a possible explanation for the cause of the error, and suggest several possible ways to give a more accurate estimate of the exposure field.

articleTitle: A novel simulation method of passive intermodulation in electrically large-size reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: As a well-known and wide-range electromagnetic compatibility problem, passive intermodulation (PIM) caused by nonlinearities remains a considerable potential risk for high-power transceiver communication systems. A three-dimensional field-circuit mixed simulation method for the prediction of PIM in electrically large-size deployable reflector antennas is presented in this work. Based on the accurate electromagnetic field calculation and an equivalent nonlinear circuit analysis, a novel simulation method for PIM analysis is proposed, which shows universality in PIM analysis of passive microwave devices. This method solves the calculation challenge caused by the dimension discrepancy between the electrical contact of nanometers and the reflector of tens of centimeters through establishing the field-to-circuit equivalent model. PIM arisen from nonlinear electrical contacts bas been modeled by an equivalent behavior model and the inaccuracy caused by the background noise and calculation error is avoided. Simulation results demonstrate that low-order PIM of a deployable reflector antenna of 15 meters is calculated successfully and match with experimental results.

articleTitle: Study on EMC of backplane interconnect system based on interference correlation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In order to solve the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problems of backplane interaction system, an advanced method based on interference correlation matrix is proposed in this paper. By building interference correlations among the ports on the backplane, the coupling relations of typical ports can be obtained. The backplane model is test to validate the simulation results and afterwards the test results go well with the simulation. In this way, different interference signals including ringing and sine wave are further analyzed to carry out EMC design among backplane channels. Finally, EMC requirements for output of modules based on interferential signals are put forward.

articleTitle: Single metal path power transfer technology without return path at 13.56MHz ISM band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Using layers of mesh shaped and flat copper plate, this paper demonstrates single metal path power transfer system without return path through the surface of aluminum foil at 13.56MHz. Transceivers are isolated from the energy propagating medium but surface wave gets excited. This technology is free from co-alignment limitation between Tx and Rx, enabling free position of Rx with given metal plate environment. Around 20% power transfer efficiency was achieved with a LC matching network part.

articleTitle: Noise isolation of PDN using in-package filter in LTCC-based system-in-package (SiP)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the noise propagation in power distribution network (PDN) of low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) based system-in-package (SiP) is studied, including the effects of printed circuit board (PCB) PDN. A low-pass filter for PDN noise isolation in LTCC-based SiP, which is made of discrete capacitors and embedded inductor, is proposed. This filter can be easily designed based on microwave-filter design theory. And it can provide broadband noise isolation along with PCB and package bulk capacitors. The electromagnetic full wave simulation results show that this method can provide noise isolation of 50dB from hundreds of kilohertz (KHz) to more than 10GHz in our case. Besides, this method can simplify PCB design by reducing ferrite beads and PCB decoupling capacitors.

articleTitle: Smart-tag EMI comparison of different program skills
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to design a low Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) software on a smart-tag system. This system is designed to collect temperature information. The information can be read by any smartphone's Near-field communication (NFC) reader. In this paper, two programs implemented by two types of methods are selected for such purpose. The first program is to get the temperature information and the second one is to send the information to an NFC transponder. The proposed methods are to implement these two programs by turning on the low-power mode or by switch the CPU into shutdown mode when idle. The measurement result shows a great EMI reduction at low-frequency range if the programs are implemented by switching CPU into shutdown mode. According to the measurement, the maximum difference is 14.38 dB at 3.2MHz for the first program and 17.68 dB at 3.2MHz for the second program.

articleTitle: Radiation physics analysis of high-speed connectors with sub-structure characteritic modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the radiation physics of edge-coupled connector is investigated with sub-structure characteristic modes and the current on the signal traces of different wafers is identified as the trouble maker for the final electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: A study on an evaluation method for EM information leakage utilizing controlled image displaying
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A method for evaluating electromagnetic (EM) information leakage through EM emanation from displays is introduced. This method judges the leakage by detecting an audio signal without needing to reconstruct the image. A leakage frequency of 140 MHz for the display was successfully obtained using a controlled image.

articleTitle: Some phase-shifterless scanning array antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Based on the general electric far-field summation, where the directions of the main beam of neighbor elements slightly differ, one can easily design a phase-shifterless scanning antenna array. Two examples are presented: elements on a circle for 360 degree scan, and an array of four horns for scanning from −22 to 22 degree.

articleTitle: Using low cost base-band digitizer for fast magnetic emission test
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Measurement time and equipment cost are main problems to be concerned about in measuring magnetic fields of equipment under test (EUT). Conventional frequency domain receiver results in long measurement time because of long dwell time per frequency step, caused by the small bandwidth. Time domain measurement is much faster. Instead of costly timedomain heterodyne analyzers, base-band sampling with low-cost digitizer is proposed. The measured data is converted to the typical results in frequency domain via fast Fourier transform with oversampling.

articleTitle: Immunity of solar inverters to transient waveforms
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper describes the impact of early-time (E1) HEMP transients on several types of solar panel inverters that are used in home solar systems. Details of the susceptibilities of several inverters and the performance of the solar systems under injection testing are provided.

articleTitle: Efficient stochastic analysis of transmission signal integrity for remote sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a statistical evaluation of the transmission signal integrity at the intra-system level of remote sensing devices. The signal integrity is evaluated using the crosstalk induced to the signal. Due to the vague knowledge of the characteristics of the signal cable, the crosstalk becomes a random quantity and needs to be described using statistics. In this paper, the stochastic reduced order model (SROM) method is applied to obtain the statistics of crosstalk in the presence of the random cable configuration. By comparing to the Monte-Carlo method, it is found that the SROM method is much more efficient and accurate. Due to the generality of the SROM method, it may be inspiring to solve other stochastic electromagnetic compatibility problems of remote sensing devices.

articleTitle: On investigation of near-field antenna for pulse-based vital-sign monitoring application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a pulsed-based vital-sign monitoring system using a comb-shaped antenna for wearable application. Two prototypes of near-field antenna are designed to investigate the performance of the received physiological signal on the wrist artery of a subject. The real-time, non-contact, and compact sensing module is analyzed, designed, and implemented.

articleTitle: Metasurfaces for specific beams generations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper concludes the recently developed several kinds of functional metasurfaces, the two-dimensional metamaterials, and then summarizes the specific beams generations based on the functional metasurfaces. Specifically, one kind of non-diffraction beams like the Bessel beam or Airy beam realized by the functional metasurface is discussed in details. Some preliminary research achievements in our group for the discussed non-diffraction beams generations are provided lastly.

articleTitle: Effects of package structure on the patch antennas with different shapes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The effects of the package structure on the patch antennas with different shapes are studied in this article. The computer simulation technology (CST) is used to design and simulate the antenna. The antenna-in-package (AiP) structure is described and two standard 5.8-GHz patch antennas with different shapes are designed. By comparing the performance of the antennas, the effects of the package structure can be understood. After the patch antenna is integrated in package, its gain and efficiency are greatly improved.

articleTitle: The dispersion relation of surface plasmon polaritons of metal bulk
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The uniform electron beam passing upon the metal bulk can excite surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs). The dispersion relation of SPPs is theoretical calculated and numerical simulated in this paper, which show that at the lower frequency regime, the dispersion curves can not match each other. It is significant for SPPs excitation at higher beam energy.

articleTitle: Aluminium feeds for reflector for NadirSAR
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: With the long term aim of developing a NadirSAR quadrotor UAV system specialized for monitoring broad acre grain fields, a large aperture load bearing antenna to use as the main structural element was sort. Here initial design work is presented on a candidate short f/D parabolic reflector antenna. An optimized splash plate feed and a dual mode coaxial horn were designed for the 10 to 10.5GHz experimenter's band and were fed by aluminum waveguide. Both feeds gave better than 30% aperture efficiency on a low cost 11.6λο diameter reflector that had a focal length of/D=0.27.

articleTitle: Verification and crosstalk of chirowaveguides
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This talk presents the numerical investigations and experimental studies on recently proposed sub-wavelength metasurface-coated chirowaveguides. Specifically, a dielectric waveguide with a single-and dual-layer metasurface coatings for enabling strong mode confinement as well as optical activity will be discussed. In addition, mode profiles for co-located chirowaveguides are examined, which reveal different crosstalk properties in E-plane and H-plane coupling configurations. It will be shown that, the designed metasurface can greatly suppress the crosstalk level even for closely located chirowaveguides.

articleTitle: The role of FSV in EMC characterization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The Feature Selective Validation (FSV) method is both a de factor and de jure standard for comparing data for validation of computational electromagnetics in the EMC domain.
