However, the “domain agnostic” approach means that it is also seeing application outside its initial area of application. The focus of development was mostly on comparisons of, or with, numerical data but the potential application to measured data was proposed but has not been fully investigated. This paper addresses radio frequency EMC characterization applications of FSV with a view to assessing its suitability for a new IEEE Standards Project, P2665, “Statistical Process Control for EMC Test Laboratories”. The conclusions are that the FSV technique may, indeed, provide a suitable objective comparison method for visually complex data or for data that requires comparison with multiple degrees of freedom but further analysis is required in order to define the clear limits of operation.

articleTitle: Amplitude characteristics of frequency band-limited LED emission for evaluation of impact on wireless medical telemeter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Statistical characteristics of the emission was investigated to evaluate an impact on a wireless medical telemeter (WMT) from LED lamp. The radiation noises from LED lamps agree well with Gaussian noise when the bandwidth is equal to that of a WMT. It can be potentially to use the average power of electric field strength when the evaluation of the interference with a WMT by LED lamps.

articleTitle: A study on nonlinear effect of modulated radio signals at 1 kHz on stimulus response
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Stimulus response caused by electromagnetic fields can be applied to medical treatments. However, it is well known that membrane potential on nerve cells has nonlinearity, so in the case of modulated signals, it is important to analyze the nonlinear stimulation effect based on a nerve cell model. In this paper, we paid attention to Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) model as the nerve cell model, and evaluated the stimulus response when nerve cells were exposed to low-frequency modulated radio signals based on the HH model. The stimulus response due to the modulated radio signals with various kinds of duty cycles and induced amplitudes were evaluated and discussed.

articleTitle: An EMC perspective of the benefits of a seawater antenna over a metal antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Compared with the metal antenna, the seawater antennas have the advantages of better stealth, stronger reconfigurability and good compatibility. In this paper, the seawater antenna system is designed, and the simulation model is established. The interference between the antennas and the RCS characteristics of the antennas are studied with different antenna dielectric. The seawater antenna's electric performance under different feed modes is also studied. The simulation results show that the RCS of the seawater antenna is smaller than metal antenna, and the compatibility between the seawater antennas is stronger than that of the metal antennas. Therefore, seawater antenna is more suitable than the metal antenna for crowed platforms. The research can provide a reference for the design of seawater antenna systems, and it can provide a new way to solve the antenna congestion problem in contempory ships.

articleTitle: Estimation of induced positions of external electromagnetic fields by measuring waveform at both ends of transmission line
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents an estimation method of induced positions of external electromagnetic fields by measuring the waveform at both ends of a transmission line. If external noise is induced in the wire harness of a vehicle, to know the induced position on the wire, it is important to measure vehicle system immunity. The wire harness is modeled as a non-uniform transmission line, and the influence positions are indirectly estimated from the measured waveforms at both ends of the transmission line. For this purpose, a time-domain equivalent circuit of the terminated non-uniform transmission line which is affected by external electromagnetic fields, is derived. Furthermore, updating formulas to calculate the time-domain characteristics for the inverse propagation problem are derived.

articleTitle: Design procedure of a CPW-fed monopole antenna for dual-band operation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a theoretical procedure of designing a coplanar-waveguide (CPW)-fed antenna for dual-band application has been presented. The stepped-impedance (SI) topology is utilized to control the resonant-band performance. By using the transmission-line analysis method, the resonance analysis of the monopole antenna is shown. The frequency-response characteristics of the SI-monopole antenna, such as the resonance condition and harmonic response, are systematically summarized.

articleTitle: In-vitro measurement system for induced voltages in medical implants in magnetic resonance imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Certification of active medical implants for use in magnetic resonance imaging machines requires the testing of immunity with respect to radiofrequency voltages induced into the active electronics of the implants. The testing of immunity is typically performed on the bench using an injection circuitry. However, the injection test voltage must be determined under real exposure conditions as they would occur in real human inside MRI. We have developed an optical differential voltage probe to be used in electromagnetically hostile environments like magnetic resonance imaging that is able to deliver the full complex-valued voltage signal with a dynamic range of 120 dB and a frequency range from 100 kHz to 1 GHz and with a total measurement uncertainty of 1.14 dB.

articleTitle: Analysis of the galvanic coupling of DC-link capacitors in a high-voltage bus of an electric car
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The passive components (cables, DC-link capacitors, air-conditioning compressor) of an exemplary high-voltage bus inside an electric car have been modeled by equivalent circuits for harmonic and transient excitation. The models have been parametrized by measurement with an impedance analyzer for the frequency range up to 1 MHz. The single models have been combined into a model for the overall system that allows to analyze the galvanic coupling and the energy flow between different DC-link capacitors at separated locations. It is found that for certain switching frequencies of the inverter, a higher current is taken from the more distant capacitor. Validating measurement have been done in the time domain with a simple inverter model.

articleTitle: Antenna diversity method for emission measurements in a reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a radiated emission measurement using an antenna diversity method in a reverberation chamber. Based on a method in the IEC 61000-4-21, a receiving antenna is rotated in three directions during the measurement.

articleTitle: Recent progress of radiated two stage method for MIMO OTA measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper firstly introduces the RTS method theory foundations, and then proposed the recent progress on the standardizations in the Cellular Telecommunication and Internet Association MIMO OTA test standard.

articleTitle: Conducted immunity of Bandgap in SOI technology after electrical stress aging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Analog circuits such as Bandgap reference circuits are crucial for electrical system operational stability. But they are very sensitive to electromagnetic interferences (EMI) which could induce voltage offset on their outputs. In harsh environments, the aging of this component can be accelerated and could lead to the changes of the effects to EMI. This paper proposes an original study about the drift of the susceptibility level of a Bandgap circuit in SOI technology submitted to electrical stresses. The measurement results show decreasing susceptibility after electrical accelerated aging.

articleTitle: Theoretical calculation and electromagnetic simulation of smith-purcell in photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: We demonstrate the Smith-Purcell (SP) effect in Photonic Crystals (PCs) excited by free electron beam. The photonic bands and equal frequency surfaces are theoretically calculated making use of the plane wave expansion method. CST PIC solver is employed to simulate SP radiation in PCs. The results reveal the special SP effect, and which may develop the new kind of vacuum electronic devcies.

articleTitle: Experiments and comparisons of power to failure for SiGe-based low-noise amplifiers under high-power microwave pulses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This study demonstrates comparisons of power to failure for SiGe-based low-noise amplifiers by injecting high-power microwave (HPM) pulses. Two types of silicon-germanium (SiGe) transistors were modeled, and their temperature distributions were simulated. The pulse thermal resistance, thermal capacitance, and breakdown temperature were calculated and determined. Results show that the power to failure of the two transistors depend on the number of slots, pulse thermal resistance, thermal capacitance, and breakdown temperature, although these transistors exhibit nearly similar structures. In addition, calculated and measured results show close correlations.

articleTitle: A study on transient current distribution caused by micro-gap ESD in spherical electrode
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Transient current distribution on electrode surface was measured when an ESD (electrostatic discharge) occurred. The transient current was measured by a shielded loop antenna. As a result of the experiment, the transient current distribution on a surface of spherical electrode showed a maximum value near the spark gap and decreased with increasing a distance from the spark gap. Furthermore, a relationship between a current path length as the distance and the peak value of the transient current was almost overlapped at the distance of 20 mm from the discharge point, regardless of the spherical electrode diameter.

articleTitle: Comprehensive signal and power co-investigation on DDR4 simulation and measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: As the technology continues to scale down and the data rate is increasing dramatically, PCB design has become more challenging than ever. Keeping track of signal and power integrity becomes a requirement for PCB designers in order to meet the product development time and reduce the overall cost. Memory is always the first component to check in a system, thus it is important to make full use of circuit and EM simulators to solve all its potential problems at the initial design stage instead of late troubleshooting. In this manner, the investigation on the DDR is studied to determine its prospective issues by SI/PI simulation. Not only the frequency domain simulation is performed to check its power integrity impedance, but the transient simulation is also applied to analyze how power integrity issue may lead to a potential signal quality failure. Simulation and measurement results are performed for verification.

articleTitle: Solutions for EM exposure assessment of 5G wireless devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A novel measurement system and a 3D field reconstruction method are described for determining the power density in the close near field of wireless devices transmitting at frequencies from 6–110 GHz. Measurements are compared against simulated results. The accuracy is better than 0.5 dB for distances greater than λ/5 from the radiating source.

articleTitle: Fast measurement of phased array antenna for 5G base station
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A novel near-field method, based on source reconstruction theory is applied to phased array antennameasurement. The efficiency of measurement can be significantly improved as compared with transitional near-field method. The far-field pattern of 5G base station antenna can be well characterized with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Measurement precision improvement to estimate the immunity performance for in-vehicle ethernet
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: It is a well-known fact that a lot of electronic control units (ECUs) and high-speed communication local area networks (LANs) are necessary for self-driving vehicle systems. Original equipment manufacturers (OEM) are interested in Ethernet that has high data rate and low signal amplitude introduced on vehicles. Thus, ensuring immunity performance is one of the main issues in the in-vehicle Ethernet. Therefore we suggested a method to define a criterion for the immunity performance using the mixed-mode S-parameter for mode conversion (Sdc11) of 100Mbps and 1Gbps Ethernet ECU. In this paper, we propose and investigate a test method using highly precise S-parameters obtained applying de-embedding technique.

articleTitle: Bias-dependent power distribution network impedance analysis with MOS capacitor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Bias-dependent power distribution network (PDN) impedance is analyzed with respect to MOS capacitor characteristics. The proposed analysis can be used to improve the PDN impedance of 2.5D and 3D ICs.

articleTitle: Partial and indirect non-reciprocal S-parameter measurement for (m + n)-port fixture with DUT
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A partial and an indirect measurement method for estimating the S-parameter of an (m + n)-port fixture and of an n-port device under test (DUT) are presented, respectively. Our model is extended to cases where the fixture and DUT are non-reciprocal, and the number m of measurement ports is less than the number n of DUT connection ports. In addition to the S-parameter between the measurement ports, the remaining diagonal elements and the product of symmetric off-diagonal elements regarding the S-parameter of the fixture and DUT are obtained. The advantage of our estimation method is that the S-parameter can be estimated by solving simultaneous linear equations and second-order algebraic equations without directly solving nonlinear equations. The proposed method can be applied to systems such as IC packages that have difficult ports to connect measuring instruments to, or cases in which circuit grounds are not common.

articleTitle: Beam switching antenna for small cell applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This article presents a novel beam switching antenna design for Small Cell applications. The proposed antenna comprises five dual-polarized dipole antenna sets, two RF switching circuit boards and one hardware control circuit board. The proposed antenna can provide wide operating band covering the 2300-2700 MHz band, and has 31 radiation pattern combinations at +45/-45° polarization individually and has dual RF ports to support 2 × 2 MIMO system. This antenna has a low profile of 76 mm, and the whole size is 200 × 200 × 76 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> that can easily mount on indoor ceiling.

articleTitle: Observation of electromagnetic noise from LED shadowless lights
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: We measured magnetic field radiation noise from light-emitting diode (LED) shadowless lights and evaluated its interference with an electromagnetic (EM) navigation system. The intensity of the magnetic field radiated from the LED shadowless lights was less than that from the EM navigation system. We confirmed that induced noise from LED shadowless lights will rarely interfere with EM navigation systems.

articleTitle: Magnetic field distribution of resonance coupling coils of wireless charging system for EV
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a 3.7kW level magnetic resonance coupling at 85kHz wireless charging system with inductor-capacitor-capacitor (LCC) network for electric vehicle is designed. The current flowing on primary and second coil are obtained in simulation by Matlab/Simlink. A pair of circular coils with ferrites are designed and modeled using 3D FEA software ANSYS Maxwell to estimate the magnetic field distribution with the vehicle body shell. The magnetic field strength at four observation points at various regions are presented to meet the level defined in SAE J2954. A pair of aluminum shield shells are designed to reduce leakage magnetic field from resonance coupling coils. The magnetic field strength with and without shielded aluminum shell are compared to validate the shielding effectiveness. The maximum magnetic field values are decreased by 23 A/m, 13.5624A/m, 8.167 A/m, 2.6043 A/m respectively. Finally, The effectiveness of the shield plate and the safety of the vehicle seat are verified by experimental test.

articleTitle: Improved topology of DC capacitors for differential mode noise mitigation in inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes improved decoupling capacitor topology in order to mitigate differential mode disturbance generated by inverter towards power supply. At first, a description of the setup used and its dedicated electrical model is made. This part allows validating the accuracy of the model. Then, frequency domain analysis is operated in order to explain each topology behavior regarding differential mode disturbance. The location of capacitors in the inverter is compared through frequency domain simulation on the one hand and experimental results on the other hand. An application is made by designing EMI filter, based on discrete LC components, and assessing efficiency involved by improved topology.

articleTitle: Optimized FPC design with EMI film
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an optimized FPC structure design method is proposed to maintain good signal integrity with EMI film. The proposed FPC design could achieve better insertion loss, return loss, and impedance control compared to common FPC designs with no extra cost.

articleTitle: Dual-band patch antenna array for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A compact antenna array consists of 2 elements dual-band patch with asymmetric coplanar waveguide (ACPW) feeding structure and a dual-band Wilkinson power divider feeding network is proposed in this article. The radiated patch was chiseled two cross-slots, there are shorted-lines to be set at the middle-and cross-points of slots, which is designed to be operated at dual-ISM band (2.4GHz and 5.8 GHz bands). A prototype of the proposed antenna with 98 mm in length, 6 mm in height and 142 mm in width is fabricated and experimentally investigated.

articleTitle: Microwave plasmonic waveguides and devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The plasmonic waveguides composed of uniform ultrathin corrugated metallic strip can support and propagate spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) with high confinement and efficiency. However, when the surface impedance of the plasmonic waveguides are modulated periodically by using non-uniform corrugated metallic strip, then the SSPPs can be converted to the radiating leaky waves, whose main beam steers continuously as frequency changes. Furthermore, by adding active components into the plasmonic waveguide, the characteristics of the SSPPs can be controlled in real time, so the devices with different functions can be realized by using only a single electrically controllable waveguide.

articleTitle: A combined 1D and 2D DGTD method for modeling multilayer power-ground planes with narrow slots
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a combined 1D and 2D Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain (DGTD) method is proposed to model multilayer power-ground (PG) planes with narrow slots. The 2D Maxwell's equations for the PG plane pairs are coupled with the Telegrapher's equations for the slots based on the surface equivalence principle. They are solved by 2D DGTD method and 1D DGTD method, respectively. The accuracy of the proposed method is validated against full-wave time-domain commercial software.

articleTitle: Simulation-based conducted susceptibility testing for wireless power transfer (WPT) systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a simulation-based conducted susceptibility (CS) testing method for wireless power transfer (WPT) systems is presented. The presented method is meant to replace the measurement-based CS testing specified in IEC 61000-4-6 standard with circuit and 3-dimensional field simulators. The conduction noise sources, propagation path, and equipment under test are modeled by the equivalent circuit models in a circuit simulator. The calibration jig dedicated to inject the standard testing noise is modeled in a 3-dimensional field solver. A wireless power transfer (WPT) system is designed to apply the presented CS testing method. The voltage and timing noise on the transferred signals and the output DC levels at the receiver are employed as criteria in the presented simulation-based CS testing method. With the presented method, time expense for the conventional measurement-based CS testing is dramatically reduced, and the testing reliability is improved without human errors that can occur in the conventional measurement-based CS testing methodology.

articleTitle: Teaching EMC using an EMC demonstration unit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: When teaching electromagnetics, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and printed circuit board (PCB) design, it is important to bridge the gap between theory and practice. This paper describes several demonstrative real-life aspects of a developed up-to-date EMC demonstration unit and contrived lab exercises. The demonstration unit proves to be useful when demonstrating EMC practices to a large variety of people, whether they are technically skilled or not. The demonstration unit also allows to realise project based teaching of future electronic design engineers.

articleTitle: Status of IEMI activities at the end of 2017
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Beginning in 1999 the concerns of Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI), as produced by new and power electromagnetic weapons, have met by considerable work by the EMC community. This work has resulted in an improved understanding of the threat through both analytical studies and experimental measurements dealing with the vulnerability of commercial equipment to these threats. This paper will begin with the early history of these studies and will emphasize the published work in recent years.

articleTitle: Circular sector antenna pair with harmonic rejection property for near-field wireless power transmission
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a circular sector antenna pair with harmonic rejection property for wireless power transmission (WPT) by near-field coupling is proposed. This antenna pair is adopted the coupled resonant method which can mutually compensate the impedance mismatching in the near field. When the transmitting antenna removes from the receiving antenna, the receiving antenna can also resonant independently and function as an antenna for Wi-Fi or energy harvesting. To improve the conversion efficiency, the circular sector antenna pair which can suppress re-radiation of the higher order harmonics to free space and reduce power loss due to the reradiation is adopted as the transmitting-receiving antenna. The conversion efficiency of the circular sector antenna pair is 80% when the input RF power is 19 dBm.

articleTitle: Some analytical formulas for the directivity calculation of antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this work we present some analytical formulas for calculating the directivity of antenna arrays, including the element patterns, positions, and weights, where the mutual coupling is ignored. A simple example is described, and is compared to simulation. The matching between the formulas and the simulation is very good.

articleTitle: Scalable platform power integrity design approach with standard PI model (SPIM) and unified PI target (UPIT)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Scalable platform power integrity design approach is first time developed, together with standard PI model (SPIM) and unified PI target (UPIT) to efficiently address HVM customers' largely design differentiation with power delivery network design & optimization, and then design review & sign-off, to flexibly make trade-off between cost and performance, or between stack-ups and PD BOM cost. Such standardized design architecture has been adopted & deployed by leading EDA tools.

articleTitle: Time-domain electromagnetic field analysis based on discrete time signal expansion and its relation to frequency domain banded signals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper we presents a novel time-domain (TD) electromagnetic (EM) field signal process by using discrete-time signal expansion. In particular, the TD signals are first expanded by a set of orthogonal basis functions which may be used to represent frequency-domain (FD) banded signals. As a result, the coefficients of TD field expansion form a matrix field in a form analogous to the EM field quantity. Thus, the conventional FD solutions for the scattering and diffraction problems can be used to predict the TD wave propagation problems. The characteristics of these TD basis functions will be investigated and presented. Examples demonstrating the applications of this technique of discrete-time signal expansion will be presented.

articleTitle: Effect of electron density in multipaction on the electromagnetic characteristics of microwave device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a theoretical model is proposed for the evaluation of effect of secondary electron density in multipaction on the electromagnetic characteristics of microwave device. Considering the distribution zone of space electron as a plasma medium, the electromagnetic characteristics of the microwave device are theoretically related to the secondary electron density in multipaction. The coaxial waveguide is simulated using the PIC tool to validate the proposed model. The reflection signal is significantly changed due to the grown of number of electrons, which provides a physical criterion for the multipaction threshold prediction.

articleTitle: Data injection attacks using a hardware Trojan on a transmission line
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we describe how an IC can be forced to process arbitrary data by using a combination of a Hardware Trojan and intentional electromagnetic interference. In addition, we discuss countermeasures against this threat.

articleTitle: Field generated by the artificial ionospheric modulation of ELF/VLF wave on the sea surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper analyses the field generated by the artificial ionospheric modulation of ELF/VLF wave on the sea surface. Ionospheric artificial modulation of ELF/VLF waves is helpful to understand the physical processes in the ionosphere, and analyze the new phenomenon. By artificially modulating the ionosphere to excite the ELF/VLF wave, the disadvantages of the traditional antenna system are overcome, such as large occupied area and difficult erection. In view of the VLF transmitter on the low earth orbit satellite, the distance between the transmitter and the underwater receiving submarine can be greatly shortened by the operation of the satellite. As a new research on submarine communication system, the transmitting and transmission of VLF waves are worth exploring. When the VLF wave transmitter carried by the satellite uses a slender antenna for the communication to submarines the slender antenna locates in the F-layer of 400km. As the simplest model, the slender antenna is idealized as an electric dipole, and the ionosphere is idealized as a homogeneous anisotropic plasma with sharp boundary. The VLF electric field on the sea surface is analyzed and calculated.

articleTitle: About the possibility of mistakes when using unipolar electric field pulses when assessing electronic device immunity to UWB pulses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: An analysis of the undesirable consequences of using unipolar waveforms of UWB electric field pulses for the assessment of the immunity of electronic devices is presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of induced voltage at close proximity with high voltage cables of electrified railways
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Cables of all types are often arranged to be installed in close proximity, including traction current carrying 3rd rail, LV and HV power cables, and telecommunication and signaling cables, in a railway system. This paper presents an analysis of the induced voltages in the victim cables under both normal and transient/fault conditions amongst cables. Approaches for the analysis of induced voltages for EMC aspects are adapted from ITU-T. Considerations of induced voltages in terms of maximum parallel length among cables for railway systems design in cable management are presented. Shielding effectiveness of metallic trunking as one of the mitigation measures is also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Dual-mode RFID tag antenna on flexible silk
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized implantable RFID tag antenna wrapped in flexible silk and applied in 920–928 MHz Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. A meandered tag antenna geometry is fed by a nested slot, where an RFID tag chip lies. The purpose of usage of flexible silk material is not only to avoid injection when being implanted (under-skin mode), but also to conduct another working mode, i.e. sticking to human body (on-skin mode). The band width of under-skin working mode is 280 MHz at 913 MHz, while reflection parameter is below −13.5 dB within ISM band in on-skin working mode. Finally, the antenna matching performance is verified by adding a body-tissue phantom into simulation.

articleTitle: Transient analysis of magnetic balance sensor with field-circuit combined simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel field-circuit combined simulation method based on Magnetic Scalar Potential Volume Integral Equation (MSP-VIE) to analyze the transient response of magnetic balance sensor. The magnetostatic field matrix information extracted by the Method of Moment (MoM) is served as the equivalent circuit parameter to construct the entire circuit model, so the field-circuit combined simulation can be uniformly implemented in the circuit solvers.

articleTitle: Fundamental study on non-invasive frequency injection attack against RO-based TRNG
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the security threat of non-invasively degrading the randomness of true random number generators (TRNGs) by injecting disturbance waves and estimating the internal state of ring oscillators (ROs) using side-channel information from outside the device. In addition, we discuss countermeasures against this type of threat.

articleTitle: Demonstration of electromagnetic waves propagation along transmission lines on iPad
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates electromagnetic (EM) waves propagation along transmission lines on iPad. The EM simulation is performed using the multiple 1-D fundamental alternating direction implicit (FADI) method, which features unconditional stability in its chosen time step for high computation efficiency. Using mobile device such as iPad, EM waves propagation along the transmission lines can be visualized in time domain while simulation is in progress. Through real time simulation, it allows engineers to carry out quick initial design and analysis of transmission lines. Furthermore, it could also help students to better understand the operating principles of various transmission lines through real-time visualizations. The demonstrated example includes transmission line loaded with open and short-circuited stubs.

articleTitle: The study of strong terahertz wave as future electromagnetic pulses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Many research institutions have paid their attentions to strong terahertz (THz) source. It is because that strong THz waves, as future electromagnetic pulses will create new challenges for the electromagnetic protection and the electromagnetic environment will become more complicated. In this research, we study the strong THz absorption in the radiation process. THz absorption is observed when preformed laser-induced air plasma and THz wave are focused at the same point. We believe that the density and collision frequency of preformed plasma is the reason for the absorption of THz. We study the THz wave frequencies during the absorption of different gas species further.

articleTitle: Immunity tests in a reverberation chamber using a correction factor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents an immunity test method using a correction factor to improve an uniformity of an E-field strength in a reverberation chamber. Based on a method in the IEC 61000-4-21, input powers are varied according to stirrer steps to create a uniform field.

articleTitle: Susceptibility of 2.4GHz low-power receivers to low frequency EMI
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper 2.4GHz ISM band Radio Frequency receivers are analyzed and tested. Electro-Magnetic Interference can couple with antennas, PCB traces and integrated inductors reaching the receiver's input and leading to communication impairment. The main causes of errors are analyzed considering the Low Noise Amplifier responsible for communication errors. Receiver susceptibility was evaluated through measurements, by injecting low-frequency interfering waveforms in the receiver front-end once the wireless communication was established. The susceptibility parameter used was the Packet Error Rate; its definition has been modified to account also for the packets lost. Vulnerability to low-frequency interference was found.

articleTitle: Analysis and experimental validation of power distribution network with multi-slots parallel-plane structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of power distribution network impedance and loop inductance of irregular parallel-plane structures and multi-slots plane-pair structures by using the plane-pair partial element equivalent circuit method(PPP). The influence of slot area occupancy rate (AOR) on impedance and loop inductance is investigated for various structures. The test structure is designed and fabricated to validate the influence of AOR on impedance and loop inductance of the PDN. The simulation and measurement of the structure impedance are performed up to 10GHz, and the good agreement are obtained between the simulation and the experiment.

articleTitle: Frequency dependent capacitance of metal semiconductor metal varactor diode and its tunable filter application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The structure of metal semiconductor metal varactor diode is presented. The capacitance dependent of the varactor on external voltage has been described. Also the frequency dependent capacitance of the varactor has been measured by Network Analyzer. We also build a tunable filter with applied bias on the varactor to investigate the frequency dependent capacitance. This shows that the capacitance reduces very fast when the frequency increases. The ratio of the capacitance from no bias to maximum bias, however, does not reduce too much. This makes the varactor useful for microwave frequency applications to protecting from electrostatic discharge, lightning, and electromagnetic pulse.

articleTitle: EMI prediction of packages by deep neural network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents advanced analysis and design methods such as the deep neural network (DNN) to predict the complex electromagnetic interference (EMI) radiation problems at the package level. Since the conventional analysis and design methods could not cope with the current EMI problems efficiently. The proposed DNN model can achieve good accuracy to predict EMI radiation.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz incabin wireless transmitting system with interference mitigation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: 2.4 GHz band is going to be congested in the aircraft, hence wireless systems using this band are highly susceptible to interference. The deployment of a wireless transmitting system using another frequency band in an aircraft cabin is investigated. The system operates at 60 GHz band with 2.16 GHz bandwidth for each channel and thus it is capable of very high throughput. Directional transmitting antennas are designed and beamforming technologies are employed, which further reduces the inference among neighboring networks.

articleTitle: A spectral fitting method for designing spectrum compatibility sequence with low correlation sidelobes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the spectrum compatibility sequence generation problem, and the sequence is required to possess the spectrum compatibility in crowded electromagnetic environments and low auto correlation sidelobes. The design problem of sequence with desired spectrum and correlation properties are formulated as the minimization of the difference between the true ones and the desired ones, respectively. Then, by introducing the time-frequency transformation, a spectral fitting method is proposed to solve it. The proposed method is based solely on FFT operations, and thus it is computationally efficient. Numerical simulations indicate that compared with the state-of-the-art algorithm, the proposed method can achieve better or equally good results with much reduced running time.

articleTitle: Synthesis of wide-band radar signals using multiple subbands in complex noise environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This talk will introduce a recently developed technique for multiple radar subbands fusion in complex noise environment. The noise considered includes the impulsive noise and the mixture of impulsive and Gaussian noises. The incoherence of the multiple subbands is first compensated by estimated incoherence factor. Ccoherent subbands are then fit by the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) model. The GTD model parameters are estimated by the sparse reconstruction method. Different types of noises are considered to simulate the real noise environment. The efficacy of the technique is shown by simulation results.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dielectric behaviour of semiconductor material under microwave field
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a microwave cavity for investigating the effect of external microwave fields on the dielectric behavior of semiconductor material is proposed. According to the Cavity perturbation technique, the measurement results shown that the dielectric properties of indium phosphate has a manifest nonlinear behavior under the high electronic field. According to effective experimental method and theoretical analysis, we conclude that the nonlinear behavior is caused by the material's inherent characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband LNA for a ship receiver system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband low noise amplifier (LNA) is designed for a ship receiver system. In a ship's communication system, the gain of 20dB is expected to be achieved to receive a weak signal within the detection range of this receiver system. By comparing the performance of different chips, the ADL5544 is selected as the amplifier unit to build a two-stage cascade structure in the LNA. In the circuit, the improved inductance capacitance structure is adopted to achieve excellent input match and output match. For better solving the problems of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), the multi-point grounding is designed in the LNA. The simulated in-band gain of the designed LNA is greater than 25dB in the whole band from 0.5GHz to 6GHz. The results of the physical measurement are slightly worse due to the circuit loss. Never the less, the LNA basically meets the engineering needs in the ship receiver system.

articleTitle: Adaptive wideband homomorphic filtering for electromagnetic interference source imaging testing system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive wideband homomorphic filtering which is directly applied to suppress the coherent noise in electromagnetic interference source imaging testing system. When the electromagnetic interference sources are coherent sources, the interference intensity of the diffraction wave is stronger than the intensity of the object point and the false detections will occur. In order to improve the quality of the image, an adaptive homomorphic filter algorithm is proposed to suppress the coherent noise in wide band. The mean square error of the system is minimized to determine the optimal parameters of the filter, and then the homomorphic transformation is used to suppress the coherence noise. The experiments result show that the proposed algorithm can successfully suppress the coherent noise in a wideband compared to the other method that does not require a high performance image sensor.

articleTitle: Radiated immunity field uniformity enhancement techniques for milli-meter wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Milli-meter wave frequencies will be used extensively in 5G wireless communication and IOT network devices. These devices could be exposed to high electromagnetic fields and must be hardened to operate and coexist in their intended electromagnetic environments, and be protected from interference and sabotage. Most of these devices would be designed with integrated antennas. Therefore, most testing must be performed Over-the-Air (OTA) and radiated immunity testing is unavoidable. However, generating and testing uniform fields over the test coverage area is complex. This document describes a theory on how the far-field test distance could be reduced and a more uniform field level can be generated over the test coverage area for any frequency range of interest. The theory is validated for mmW frequencies using measured test data.

articleTitle: Analysis of the accuracy and limitation of contour integral equation modeling of planar structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents the derivation of contour integral equation (CIE) modeling of planar structures based on field quantities and equivalence principle. It is shown that the CIE derived based on field quantities is essentially the same as the one derived based on voltages and currents. The derivation of CIE based on field quantities provides better understanding of the assumption of CIE, and thus allows easy analysis of the accuracy and limitation of CIE. Simulations are performed to evaluate the validity of the assumptions, and the accuracy of CIE is investigated.

articleTitle: An ultrathin wideband capsule antenna with low level specific absorption ratio
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturization antenna with stable impedance matching for Wireless capsule endoscope over 1.4GHz Wireless Medical Telemetry Services (WMTS) is proposed only on 0.05mm flexible substrate. In order to achieve impendence matching, inversed T matching branch is employed. Moreover, current vector alignment and conductor coupling factors are used to decrease antenna effective dimensions. Fresh pork is applied to simulation the human body in practice. The input impendence, gain, bandwidth, radiator efficient, SAR value are discussed in detail. Communication links between the proposed and external receiving antennas in different orientations and distance are measured. Simulation and measurement results show that the conformal antenna has a maximum simulated gain of −26.3 dBi (homogeneous muscle) and a minimum gain of −38.57 dBi (small intestine). The maximum impedance bandwidth is 111MHz (7.9%) in a homogeneous muscle phantom.

articleTitle: An improved multi-level weighting additive summation method for electromagnetic compatibility evaluation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility evaluation is an important technical measure in the ship design and efficiency evaluation, and guarantees the electron equipment and electric equipment be work together without any performance decline. This paper analyzes the present evaluation methods' disadvantages, and brings forward an improved multi-level weighting additive summation method. This method adopts standard deviation weighing measure distributing weigh, which belongs to external investiture weigh and avoids subjective because of lack of uniform external criterions. Improved multi-level weighting additive summation method normalizes the quantificational technical target and make qualitative technical target impersonal. This method solves the evaluating problem in complex target system of multi-object, multi-level, asymmetry, and multi-conditionality. To validate the improved method, one design proposals for a particular platform model are evaluated. The results indicate that the presented approach is suitable for analyzing complicated systems. This method has preferable engineering value and directive sense.

Author Keywords: improved multi-level weighting additive summation method

articleTitle: Extraction of equivalent impedance of photovoltaic panel under its actual operating conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is a growing concern for the implementation of photovoltaic (PV) systems. Widespread use of PV panels with high switching frequency power converters can result in significant EMI emission. Hence, an accurate circuit model of the PV panel under its actual operating condition is necessary so that the impact of impedance variation of the PV panel on EMI can be better evaluated. In this paper, an in-circuit measurement based method is adopted to extract the necessary parameters of the impedance model of the PV panel to facilitate the study of its impedance variation on EMI in the frequency range of interest.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic interference evaluation at myoelectric signal detector for robot control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we quantitatively evaluated the EMI of a myoelectric signal detector used in robot control. We measured the EMI voltages at the output of the myoelectric signal detector for a given common-mode noise between the human body and the earth ground, and clarified the relationship between the EMI voltage and frequency as well as imbalance between the contacting resistances of sensing electrodes.

articleTitle: Probe calibrations for phased array measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Near-field measurements have many advantages over the conventional far-field measurements in the phased array measurements. Source construction is an improved measurement technique with the test range between near-field and far-field measurement. Probe correction have been generally studied in all near-field scanning methods. Yet, probe calibrations techniques are not discussed for phased array measurements. In this paper, probe calibrations techniques for phase array measurements will be presented. With probe corrected calibration, the phased array and the probes are not treated as phase-center points, and higher measurement accuracy is achieved.

articleTitle: Differential-skew mitigation by rotating meshed ground
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The asymmetry, or imbalance, of a differential-transmission-line pair over a meshed ground plane depending on their position leads to the differential skew. This study is focused on the angle between the differential-transmission-line pair and the meshed ground to investigate the angle dependence of differential skew. In a full-wave simulation after preliminary evaluation by a simple model, it is found that the differential skew does not depend on the position of the differential transmission lines to the pattern of the meshed ground and keeps a comparatively small value at the rotation angle around 30°.

articleTitle: Development of spacecraft radiated susceptibility RS103 requirements from modeling methods
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In defining radiated susceptibility requirements for a spacecraft with multiple number of receivers and transmitters in close proximity to each other, the main objective of an RF coupling analysis is to determine if the mechanical configuration of the receiver and transmitter antennas presents a risk to the functionality and safety of sensitive science instruments on the payload as a result of unintended RF coupling. Where there is a potential risk for interference or permanent damage, further analysis is required to evaluate the feasibility of mitigation schemes, such as mechanical reconfiguration of antennas or additional RF filtering. From these coupling analysis results, radiated susceptibility RS103 requirements are derived to better reflect actual requirement levels with adequate test margins.

articleTitle: Measured MIMO throughput under different transmit power of DUT
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The effect of noise is one of the most important considerations when evaluating the receiver performance of wireless systems. In multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) OTA measurements, different kinds of device hold different maximum power levers and may be tested in different transmit power, as the power lever effects the physical temperature and then increase the noise temperature, the measurement will result in relative uncertainty when conducting MIMO throughput measurement. This paper illustrates the relationship between measured MIMO throughput and transmit power levels of device under test in order to evaluate the MIMO receiver performance and optimize the design.

articleTitle: A statistical equivalent circuit modelling based on measured and de-embedded S-parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a statistical equivalent circuit model of a chip monolithic ceramic capacitor is analyzed based on the measured and de-embedded S parameters. By optimizing the model parameters in the equivalent model, the deviation introduced by the measurement and the de-embedding process are alleviated. Through analyzing the equivalent model of 1pF and 2pF capacitor, the model of a 1.5pF capacitor is calculated and verified by the measurement results.

articleTitle: Bended differential transmission lines using asymmetric stepped-impedance lines for common-mode noise suppression
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a bended differential transmission lines using asymmetric stepped-impedance lines is proposed to eliminate differential-to-common mode conversion and common-mode noise. The bended differential transmission lines using asymmetric stepped-impedance lines can reduce the differential-to-common mode conversion from −29.8 dB to −41.4 dB and the common-mode noise from 0.0051 V to 0.0035 V as compared with the bended differential transmission lines using stepped-impedance lines. In order to verify the simulation results, measurement is done in the frequency and time domains where the measurement results are in good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Common mode noise analysis of buck-boost converter for hybrid energy storage systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Under the influence of high speed power switch device, electromagnetic interference (EMI) affects heavily the normal operation of the buck-boost circuit in hybrid energy storage system (HESS). In this paper, the working principle of the buck-boost converter in hybrid energy storage system is analyzed, and the relationship between common-mode (CM) voltage and the voltage of switching device is obtained. By analyzing the frequency spectrum of the voltage of switching device, the relationship between the switching characteristics and the system conducted electromagnetic interference is proposed, and the prediction model of the conducted electromagnetic interference for hybrid energy storage system is established. In addition, the mechanism of ringing and overshoot during switching time of switching devices is studied and reduced by the method of adding capacitor, and experimental results validate the analysis method.

articleTitle: Mode analysis of adjacent differential-paired lines using extended mixed-mode S-parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In the adjacent differential-paired lines, the balanced differential lines in one pair become weak imbalanced due to the coupling with the differential lines in another pair. As a result, the common-mode currents become unequal on the imbalanced differential lines. In this new mode analysis, the current division factors are adopted to divide the common mode currents on the imbalanced differential lines. Furthermore, the mode conversion between the extended mixed-mode S-parameters and the standard S-parameters of the adjacent differential-paired lines is developed based on the new mode analysis. The good agreement between the simulated and converted extended mixed-mode S-parameters verified the effectiveness of the new mode analysis proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: A simulation and experimental study of the failure of an internal digital clock due to ESD and its mitigation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents the diagnosis and mitigation of ESD failure due to internal digital clocks, in contrast to asynchronous/control signals conventionally. A combined simulation approach with 3D electromagnetic and circuit simulation is developed to capture the coupled ESD waveforms. It is validated with measurement data and good agreement is obtained. A filter comprised of a ferrite bead and shunt capacitor is demonstrated to improve the ESD robustness of a laptop system from 2 KV to 12 KV. This work may be employed to facilitate debugging of ESD issues and to improve ESD robustness.

articleTitle: Common mode conversion noise suppression using L-Pad with asymmetric coupled lines on bended differential lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Right-angle bended differential lines using L-Pad with asymmetric coupled lines (ACL) are proposed to suppress the differential-to-common mode conversion. The L-pad with ACL not only suppresses the mode conversion noise effectively, but also has advantages on using in practical printed circuit board (PCB) layout because it does not occupies additional PCB areas. The simulated results show that differential-to-common mode noise conversion of proposed structure is maintained under −20 dB from DC to 4.98 GHz while conventional right-angle bended differential lines provides −20 dB suppression levels only up to 1.12 GHz. Also, Time Domain Transmission (TDT) common mode noise voltage is simulated and compared with other structures. The proposed design shows significant suppression of common mode noise with 42 mV, while other structures with compensation capacitance and with only L-pad show 118 mV and 88 mV respectively. Finally, measured results are compared with simulated results and show good agreements.

articleTitle: Ultralow-noise isolated switch-mode power supply
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: We present an adjustable isolated power supply, with an RMS noise less than 30μV.

articleTitle: Planar hybrid common mode filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This work presents a design combining an electro-magnetic bandgap structure with periodically shaped differential signal lines for the suppression of common mode noise. This hybrid design is compared against two individual layout structures and a regular reference line. Besides the common mode rejection also the mode conversion is considered.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic emissions from GaN power IC at varying distance and frequency
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic emissions (EME) from Integrated Circuits (ICs) is increasing due to rapid increase in their operating frequencies and layout complexity. Near field analysis is one of the most common and effective method to measure EME. In this work, magnetic field and electric field of IC is analyzed at various distances from the surface of IC through simulation model. It is found that the magnetic field is major source of emission in vicinity of IC than electric field. It is also found that the location of maximum emission of magnetic field varies with the change in frequency as well. This work helps in determining the optimum distance between the adjacent devices to keep the EME in check.

Author Keywords: Gallium Nitride (GaN) High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT)

articleTitle: Time domain measurement of collision ESD using optical E-Field sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The robustness of electrostatic discharge of electronic devices has declined with the increase in operation frequency and performance of the system. As a countermeasure against the problem, development of protection technology is urgently required, and detailed observation of discharge phenomena is required. In this study, Time domain measurement of collision ESD using optical E-Field sensor was studied.

articleTitle: Development of wealable ECG based on human body communication technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In daily healthcare monitoring, wearable electro-cardiogram (ECG) with wireless function is essential because it is easy to use and helpful to early detection of cardiac diseases. However, various electromagnetic (EM) interference issues need to be solved for its normal use. In this study, we developed a wearable ECG which employs the extremely weak radio band and a wideband human body communication (HBC) technology. The realized wireless function provides higher anti-interference performance and more reliable ECG signal acquisition, compared to usually used Bluetooth technology at 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Equivalent sources approach on radiation performance evaluation of personal wireless devices with head and hand phantom
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The radiation performance evaluation of personal wireless device (mobile phone, laptop, tablet etc.) with head and hand phantom (Talk Mode) is widely performed with the increase of the quantities, communication services and the frequency bands of wireless products. This lead to a considerable requirement of measurement systems on all stages of the product life: R&D, production, certification, sales and after-sales. Equivalent sources approach is proposed on these radiation performance evaluation scenarios in Near-Field(NF), while traditional Far-Field(FF) methods remain several drawbacks e.g. needing a large anechoic chamber, which is cost-inefficient. The method mentioned may solve the problem of radiation performance evaluation of wireless devices at this stage or the coming 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation.

articleTitle: Practical considerations of human exposure in railway systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents some practice considerations in human exposure, together with related safety aspects in ICNIRP, in hearing aids and body wearable medical devices in railway systems. On-board traction power and harmonic currents in the third rail are sources commonly encountered for human exposure, their compliance approach and related EMC requirements are discussed and summarized.

articleTitle: EMC simulation of automotive ethernet systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This presentation deals with the analysis of conducted and radiated emissions of Automotive Ethernet systems by using a combination of full wave 3D field analyses and circuit simulations. Performing such simulations at an early stage of product development may give valuable answers regarding the EMC performance of the electronic design. Since PCBs, connectors, and cables individually influence the electromagnetic emission, a thorough understanding of the common mode effects in all of these components is key for a compliant system design. In this presentation, we discuss and demonstrate several countermeasures for common mode currents in order to suppress the emission.

articleTitle: Fast conical-cut radiation measurement by using lens fed reflector for 5G antenna application at mmW frequencies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper describes an antenna measurement system by using a lens fed reflector to fast meaasure the conical-cut patterns of antenna radiation at millimeter wave (mmW) frequencies for 5G applications. In particular, the pattern measurement is sequentially performed in a progressive fashion by using a 6-axes robotic arm to vary the angles of conical cut along the theta arc in the spherical coordinate system. This rotation mechanism accelerates the measurement speed with accurate phase center estimation in comparison to conventional measurement approaches. In our implementation, the quiet zone (QZ) of 3 × 3 cm has been achieved by using a 9.5 × 8.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> oval-shape refelctor fed by a lens antenna at 38 GHz.

articleTitle: Safety aspects of LTE wearable antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Wearable Antenna for High Power Applications in 700–2200 MHz band is presented. The expected radiation exposures for the antenna carrier are discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of coupling coefficient on transmission and reflection zeros of open-ended coupled ideal stubs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of the coupling coefficient on the reflection zero (RZ) and transmission zero (TZ) of the open-ended parallel transmission line (TL). The structure is assumed equivalent to ideal coupled parallel stub (CPS). Theoretical circuit approach is considered to establish the frequency-dependent reflection and transmission coefficient expressions. The CPS RZ and TZ formulas in function of the coupling coefficient are derived. The CPS RZ and TZ characterizations in function of the elementary TL TZs and coupling coefficient are described. The relevance of the established CPS analytical model was effectively verified with microstrip structures operating in the frequency band 0.1 GHz to 10 GHz and the coupling coefficient varied from -20 dB to -0.9 dB. Excellent correlation between the introduced CPS model and the considered ideal CPS structure simulations was found in function of the coupling coefficient. The elaborated circuit theory is potentially useful for the printed circuit board (PCB) design, electromagnetic interference (EMI) and signal integrity engineering.

articleTitle: Simulations of railway VCB switching noise
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A hybrid modeling method based on a combination of 3D and 2D simulations as well as circuit simulations has been proposed, in order to investigate the main coupling path of the vacuum circuit breaker switching noise and to explain its dependence on the infrastructure.

articleTitle: A novel hybrid 2D/Q-2D finite element method for power/ground plane analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: By realizing the TMz modal distribution property between the power/ground plate-pairs, the magnetic field actually has only azimuthal components while longitude component is zero. Thus, if the magnetic field wave equation is solved, only a Quasi-2D issue is considered. Furthermore, since the high-order modes are only located in the near region of the anti-pad, thus for the domain far-away from the antipad has only the TEM mode. Thereby, in this region, the magnetic field is invariable along the vertical direction, which consequently is a pure 2D domain. As a result, the conventional 3D computational domain is naturally transformed to a hybrid 2D/Q-2D domain, which will significantly reduce the computational cost.

articleTitle: Bulk current injection quantification of BroadR-Reach® protocol based system by measurements and modeling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: BroadR-Reach® is a point-to-point Ethernet Physical Layer standard for automotive applications, allowing full-duplex communication between two devices over an unshielded twisted-wire pair (UTP) at 100 Mb/s. The high transmission speed in combination with the use of an unshielded harness makes compliance of the BroadR-Reach® Ethernet with automotive Electromagnetic Compatibility requirements a challenging task. This paper investigates the main factors influencing the outcome of Bulk Current Injection (BCI) tests carried out on BroadR-Reach® Ethernet channels. To this end, experimental measurements, circuit and electromagnetic simulation of a simplified test setup are exploited. The analysis allows putting in evidence the fundamental role played by line length, injection probe positioning, and imbalance affecting the terminal units, as well as the impedance discontinuities introduced when the UTP has to be interfaced with a shielded (untwisted) wire-pair (SWP) of the fiber optics converter electronics.

articleTitle: Small left-handed balun designed to increase MIMO antenna isolation for AP systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to handle the isolation problem of a MIMO antenna for Wi-Fi access point(AP). Firstly, a quasi-Yagi antenna is designed with a transmission-line balun at the feed. Secondly, this conventional quasi-Yagi antenna is adopted for the two closely placed MIMO elements for 2.4 GHz-AP equipment, and the coupling between them is checked. The 180° delay-line of one element is long and next to the feed of the other element, which is an obstacle to the isolation improvement. Hence, the conventional balun is replaced by right and left-handed phase shifters, which take up a much smaller area of the feed and result in improved isolation. In addition, the MIMO radiating elements based on the metamaterial phase-shifters show less inclination of the main beam from the intended direction. The MIMO quasi-Yagi antennas without and with the metamaterial phase-shifter balun are designed, and their return-loss, beam-patterns and isolation curves are compared. Also, the full-wave simulation results are given with the measured ones.

articleTitle: Shielding effectiveness estimation for shielding box having unknown aperture
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents an estimation method to obtain shielding effectiveness (SE) of a shielding box. The estimation method can be applied even when an aperture on the surface of the shielding box is unknown.

articleTitle: Time-domain coupling analysis of unequal length MTLs excited by plane wave
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a time domain hybrid method consisting of transmission line (TL) equations, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, and a S-parameter cascade technique to be used for the coupling analysis of unequal length multi-conductor transmission lines (MTLs) excited by plane wave efficiently. In this method, the FDTD-TL method is used to compute the transient responses on each equal length MTLs. The signal transmission between the equal length MTLs are realied by the S-parameters of the nodes.
