Numerous examinations have been used to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of this method by compared with the traditional FDTD method.

articleTitle: Non-ionizing EMF hazard in the 21th century
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: With the fast advancement in technologies and the heavy reliance on wireless devices, we are exposed to ever increasing electromagnetic field (EMF) radiation from home to office to public places. The two most widely referenced standards for non-ionizing EMF radiation protection - IEEE C95.1 and ICNIRP - were last updated in 2005 and 1998 respectively. A comparison of the two standards with the Russian standard shows that the Russian maximum permissible exposure (MPE) is 41 and 5.8 times lower in terms of electric field strength at 1MHz respectively. Despite numerous tests showing potential hazards to humans from radiation levels below the MPE levels stated in ICNIRP guidelines and C95.1, ICNIRP and IEEE continue to ignore calls by scientists to review their MPE levels. This paper addresses the current and future trends in communication and wireless technologies and their impact on the EMF radiation level that the general public will be exposed to. Studies on biological effects due to EMF radiation carried out over the last 20+ years will also be discussed. Based on the effects of these studies from radiation levels well below the MPE in C95.1 and ICNIRP guidelines, this paper recommends a review of the current safety levels.

articleTitle: Enforcing correlation between conducted and radiated susceptibility test setups for aerospace involving shielded cables
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A conducted-susceptibility test procedure based on Bulk Current Injection (BCI) is designed to reproduce similar levels of interference occurring in a standard radiated-susceptibility (RS) test setup for aerospace equipment involving shielded cables. The correlation between test levels is accounted for by an engineering margin called overtesting (OT), which quantifies the excess of interference injected by BCI over RS. Owing to the lack of knowledge about the common-mode impedance of equipment, as well as other setup-related uncertainties, OT turns out to be a random variable, here characterized through its cumulative distribution function. The proposed approach is experimentally validated and complements results developed earlier for unshielded cables. As far as achievement of correlation between BCI and RS tests is concerned, distinctive features of shielded (vs unshielded) cables are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Emission reduction with spread spectrum clocking for switched capacitor buck converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The reduction of electromagnetic emissions (EME) in switch mode power supplies (SMPS) has high importance especially in automotive applications. The main methods to influence the switching behaviour of SMPS are external filters, spread spectrum techniques and output driver circuits. This paper presents the application of the spread spectrum technique for a 1.25 V and 1.851 MHz switched capacitor buck converter with a digital control loop to reduce the conducted emissions. The frequency modulated sawtooth and pseudo-random profiles are implemented in the digital controller and discretized by a 100 MHz system digital clock. The work investigates the influence of the profile's modulation frequency and the effect of the pulse width modulation (PWM) resolution limitation on the EME reduction. The improvement using a sawtooth profile of 10 dBuV in comparison to the non-modulated PWM signal is seen and discussed. The comparison between modulated and non modulated output voltage ripple is also presented.

articleTitle: A full time domain methodology based on near field time reversal for equivalent source identification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper deals with magnetic source characterization in time domain. The basic idea is to solve the inverse problem using the measured near field radiation cartography. In order to ensure the identification procedure, the Time Reversal (TR) technique is used. This procedure allows both the spatial and temporal focusing determination by forcing waves to virtually converge to their initial source. The originality of the proposed methodology is to present a full time domain study of a magnetic source reconstruction. Indeed, this approach is particularly suitable for structures that emit non-sinusoidal radiations such as power electronic systems. First, the Electromagnetic Time Reversal (EMTR) basis are introduced. Then a simulation case study is discussed. Finally, results from an experiment test are presented to verify the proposed methodology. The measured results are in good agreement with the calculated electromagnetic fields. The experimental validation shows that compared to other identification techniques, especially those developed in the frequency domain, the proposed approach is more efficient and simple.

articleTitle: An analytical approach for DC-link DM filter design for PM AC motor drives
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed procedure for DC-Link Differential Mode filter design for AC Permanent Magnet Motor Drives. The goal is to design a filter to attenuate Differential Mode noise, caused by PWM controlled motor load current, below specified limits. The specified limits are defined by DO-160 Section 21 or MIL 461 CE102. Analytical calculation is used to estimate DC-Link current harmonics based on motor parameters and load conditions. Once unfiltered DC-Link current harmonics defined, the filter Insertion Loss (IL) can be estimate to comply with above standards. All analytical results are compared with the results of PSPICE and MATCAD analysis.

articleTitle: Digital-domain assisted RF cancellation of nonlinear wideband self-interference for co-site wireless communication systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a digital-domain assisted radio-frequency (RF) cancellation architecture is proposed to cancel the nonlinear wideband self-interference (SI) signal for co-site communication systems. First, a cancellation chain is introduced to reconstruct and suppress the SI signal received at the receiver chain. Then, we derive two nonlinear models with the Hammerstein model and Wiener model employed for the transmit chain, respectively. The proposed models can predicate the SI coupling characteristics, which include the transmit chain and wireless channel, more accurately for the nonlinear wideband SI signal. Next, the coefficients of both linear and nonlinear component in the SI chain are integrated into a signal vector, which is linear with respect to the output samples. Therefore, simple least-squares (LS) algorithm is adopted in the estimation of model coefficients by taking the linearity of the proposed models. Finally, experimental results validated that the proposed scheme has a superior interference cancellation performance for nonlinear wideband self-interference.

articleTitle: Prediction of common mode current in cable harnesses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Common mode current on cable harnesses is often responsible for system level EMI, but is difficult to predict early in the design process. Typical component level measurements are unhelpful as common mode currents may change dramatically when the component is placed in the system. A methodology is developed in the following paper to estimate common mode current in system-level applications based on component-level measurements. Estimates are made by assuming that termination impedances can be approximated as shorts or opens with respect to the characteristic impedance of the harness. Furthermore, the dominate sources of common mode current for each set of terminations (open or short) should have similar source impedances. With these assumptions, the common mode current on the harness can be approximated from the sum of currents on two equivalent circuits terminated with an open and a short. The source characteristics of each equivalent circuit can be determined from two measurements of common mode current on harnesses of two different lengths. The equivalent circuits can be used to estimate common mode currents on harnesses of arbitrary length and characteristic impedance.

articleTitle: The shielding effect of a multi-cable harness as function of IC output termination impedance
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Integrated circuits for automotive applications must not violate certain limits for maximum electromagnetic emissions. One of many standardized compliance tests is the CISPR 25 ALSE test, where the radiated emission from a straight cable harness attached to a device is evaluated. For devices with multiple outputs this harness may contain multiple cables. It is critical to understand, that non-operated cables have a certain shielding effect, which is a function of their termination impedance. The radiated emission originating from a harness consisting of multiple cables will, in some cases, be drastically lower than that of a single wire. By applying fundamental electrostatic relations this paper demonstrates how to estimate the deviation by simple calculations. The analytical results are compared to measurements and 3D EM simulation.

articleTitle: Estimation for S-parameters of a differential communication transceiver IC applying an indirect measurement method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A method to estimate the multiport S-parameters of an IC device mounted on a PCB is proposed. This method is useful to obtain the actual S-parameters in operating environment. Our previously proposed indirect measurement methods for S-parameters of multiport circuit with some of its ports not directly measured are combined and organized as a self-contained method to estimate the whole S-parameters of multiport-connection consisting of PCB traces and wires. Here, measurement instrument is connected through the multiport-connection and the S-parameters of the target IC device is obtained from the measured result by de-embedding the indirect-measured multiport-connection S-parameters. An example is shown in detail when applied to an actual automotive LAN transceiver IC and its prototype PCB to evaluate the potential of this method up to 1.5GHz.

articleTitle: Feasibility of uncertainty quantification for power distribution network modeling using PCE and a contour integral method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This work presents the modeling of the printed circuit board part of power distribution networks (PDNs) and example results for the uncertainty quantification for the magnitude of the corresponding impedance. Variability is considered for several parameters, including geometry, material properties, and the models of the decoupling capacitors. For the computation of the parallel plate impedance an efficient and accurate two-dimensional contour integral method (CIM) is applied together with models for the wave number for the complete frequency range of interest. Polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) is used in the non-intrusive form of stochastic testing for the uncertainty quantification and Monte Carlo simulations are used for the validation of these results. To our knowledge this combination of methods represents the first application of CIM and PCE to the modeling of PDNs. The PCE is found to be numerically more efficient than Monte Carlo in cases where parameters are varied that have an influence on the parallel plate impedance. It can be less efficient for variation of only the models of decoupling capacitors. It is applicable if not too many parameters are varied at a time and accurate if resonance effects due to low-loss substrate materials and components are not too pronounced at the considered frequency.

articleTitle: Comparison of two setups for contactless power measurements for side-channel analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: When performing side-channel analysis of (passively powered) contactless devices such as RFID tags the side-channel signal is dominated by the carrier field used to power the device. This carrier field should be removed by the measurement setup in order to expose the power consumption of the target device and enable a side-channel analysis. In this paper we describe and compare two methods for measuring the power consumption of contactless devices. The comparison is done experimentally by running applets on a contactless BasicCard and evaluating the signal to noise ratio of the measurements collected with each setup. Our results show that both setups perform similar, indicating that more research is needed to investigate the differences and strengths.

articleTitle: Conducted and radiated interference on the interconnections of renewable energy farms
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic disturbances are usually classified into conducted and radiated disturbances, which are rather loosely defined. That causes confusion among the people that work in the area, in different time scales. In this paper we put forward a formulation of the electromagnetic coupling, based on the potentials, that, when the matter is described by constitutive laws, is valid in any time scale, thus providing a common framework to study conducted and radiated interferences. We show that, for a transmission line, the electromagnetic field can be separated in two independent modes: a longitudinal TM mode and a transversal TE mode. We also show that the scattered field is a longitudinal TM mode and that, for usual transmission lines, the longitudinal mode can be described by Kirchhoffs laws. We show that the conducted disturbances are just a common longitudinal mode; while the radiated disturbances can conveniently be divided into a longitudinal mode and a transversal mode. For the longitudinal mode, its effect can be represented as a voltage or current source, and, the effect of the transversal mode is just to produce an induced voltage between the conductors. Finally, we present some application examples to illustrate the usefulness of this interpretation.

articleTitle: Reducing functional safety and other risks due to EM disturbances: IEEE Standard 1848
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: IEEE Standard 1848 (draft) deals with the problem of managing safety and any other kinds of risks that could be caused by electromagnetic disturbances. It is impractical to test digital hardware or software sufficiently thoroughly for the low levels of risk required for functional safety-related applications, so this is the first of a new type of EMC standard which has requirements that go well beyond immunity testing. This paper describes these issues, and how this new IEEE standard will achieve its aims. It is an improved and updated version of a paper first presented at the 2016 IEEE EMC Symposium in Ottawa.

articleTitle: Extending the normal immunity tests to help prove functional safety
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Functional Safety requires very low levels of safety risks. Where this is achieved at least partly by the use of a programmable electronic safety-related system, electromagnetic disturbances are a cause of risks so must be taken fully into account in the risk management process. However, it is not practicable to rely solely on the normal immunity tests, at whatever test levels, to demonstrate that such risks will be low enough throughout the lifecycle. Instead, a number of different verification/validation techniques should be applied, including (but not limited to) immunity testing. This paper describes modified immunity test methods that provide verification/validation additional to that provided by standard immunity tests. It is an improved and updated version of a paper originally presented at the 2016 International IEEE EMC Symposium held in Ottawa, Canada.

articleTitle: Fields and current densities induced in the human body by low-frequency electromagnetic fields
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Up to now, there seems to be a confusion concerning the description of the interaction of matter with an external electromagnetic field or with extraneous (injected) charges. In this paper we show that an electromagnetic field interacting with matter must be described by four vector fields (E, H, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> and B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>). For non-magnetic matter only three fields are necessary (E, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> and B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>). The field Be has two parts: the first is the displacement D, which is locally proportional to E; and the second is M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">efr</sub>, which represents the existence of free electric carriers within the matter. For time-harmonic low-frequency fields, if σ/ωε >> 1, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> is dominated by M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">efr</sub>, which depends on the history of E. Then, inside the human body, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> is locally proportional to E delayed by 90 degrees. In the case of a polarized external field, this delay has the consequence that, at the points inside the human body, at a certain time instant, E and B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> do not even have the same direction.

articleTitle: Modeling the internal activity of an FPGA for conducted emission prediction purpose
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: End-users of integrated circuits need models to anticipate and solve conducted emission issues at board level in a short time. This is the purpose of the standard IEC62433-2 ICEM-CE. Although it proposes methods to extract circuit models from measurements, they cannot provide activity dependent models and may lead to inaccurate results for large and complex circuits. This paper describes a new methodology of construction of the internal activity block of an ICEM-CE model adapted to large digital integrated circuits and validated on a FPGA. The method is based on a predictive approach using the estimation tools of the dynamic power and the data path delays proposed by the manufacturer of the integrated circuit.

articleTitle: Risk management of electromagnetic disturbances
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: It is sometimes necessary to manage Functional Safety or other risks throughout the lifecycle of an electronic system. All electronics can be affected by electromagnetic (EM) disturbances, therefore such systems must take EM disturbances into account when managing risks. Modern digital electronics are so very complex, and the risk levels associated with Functional Safety are so small, that immunity testing is totally inadequate as the sole method of risk verification or validation. The IEC's `Basic Safety Standard' on Functional Safety requires a risk-based approach to managing electromagnetic interference (EMI), and many product-family functional safety standards have been published with this requirement. None of these standards contained any detailed requirements for dealing with EM disturbances, which were first published as practical guidance by the IET in 2013. This guidance - the subject of this paper - is now being incorporated into IEC, IET and IEEE standards. This paper is an improved and updated version of a paper first presented at the 2016 IEEE EMC Symposium in Ottawa.

articleTitle: Analysis of conducted-EMI noise influence on the effectiveness of an EDAC technique to mitigate soft errors in ionizing radiation environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This work describes preliminary experiments that analyze the influence of conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) noise on the effectiveness of an error detection and correction (EDAC) technique. This technique was originally conceived to mitigate multiple-bit upsets (MBUs) or soft errors in memory elements (flip-flops and SRAM cells) of integrated circuits (ICs) operating in heavy ions environment. The analysis was performed on a Microsemi ProASIC3E A3PE1500 FPGA, which was operating in an 8MV Pelletron heavy-ion accelerator while exposed to conducted EMI noise on IC input power port. Injected noise comprised of voltage dips of 19.6% of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</sub> at the frequency of 5kHz and was performed according to the IEC 61000-4-29 standard. The obtained results suggest that the proposed technique is very effective to detect and correct multiple bit flips induced by the combined effects of ionizing radiation and conducted EMI on the tested IC input power port.

articleTitle: Lightning protection and EMC issues of renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The paper reviews lightning protection and EMC issues for renewable energy sources systems. Based on lightning risk management concept, optimal lightning protection schemes for wind turbine generation systems and photovoltaic generation systems are considered. EMC issues are also considered.

articleTitle: A multi-tone interference equivalence method for analyzing the impact of LFM interference on the BER of communications data link system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The Direct Spread Communications Data Link System (CDLS) bears strong Linear Frequency Modulation (LFM) interference from collocated radars, which makes it necessary to analyze the influence of the LFM interference on the performance of CDLS. LFM interference has both the characteristics of an instantaneously single-tone and cumulatively multi-tone signals. For this reason, the derivation of an analytic Bit Error Rates (BER) formulation is difficult. This paper presents a BER model that can transform calculation of the BER under LFM interference into the BER under equivalent multi-tone interference, and then derive the equivalence factor between the two. We conduct simulations to analyze the impact of the single-tone and multi-tone as well as LFM interference on the BER of CDLS. Then, we verify the equivalence relationship between LFM interference and multi-tone interference with different center frequencies and FM modulation coefficients. The simulation results show that the equivalence error is less than 2.5% when the BER is higher than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, which is the typical case of CDLS. The LFM interference equivalence BER calculation method proposed in this paper can quantify the equivalence coefficient, and accurately reflect the influence of LFM interference on the BER of CDLS, which contributes to the research of effective analysis of the interference mechanism of CDLS.

articleTitle: Analysis of field-to-transmission line coupling inside a reverberation chamber based on mode expansion method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic (EM) field distribution inside a reverberation chamber (RC) is constructed by Monte Carlo simulation based on mode expansion method (MC_MEM). This method provides the position information of sampling points inside a RC based on mode theory of resonant cavities. Then the current responses of a single transmission line (TL) with terminal loads located inside a RC are calculated to verify the effectiveness of MC_MEM. By comparing current responses of different TL structures, the statistical uniformity of EM field distribution inside a RC can be illustrated. And these results could provide more information about EM environment inside RC and some guidelines for TLs arrangement.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave propagation measurement during rainy days in Beijing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: High-quality, and long-term observation of environmental conditions (e.g. rainfall and water vapour) at fine temporal and spatial resolution is of great important to meteorology, hydrology (e.g. flood warning), agriculture, environmental policy (e.g. pollution regulation) and weather forecasting. This work will discuss the potential of using future millimeter wave based cellular networks for facilitating the high resolution and intensive environmental monitor in the near future, particularly for rainfall monitoring.

articleTitle: Automated equivalent circuit extraction of impedance curves using a Gauss-Newton algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this study, an algorithm has been implemented to automate the extraction of passive component values from impedance curves. The method has been applied to a Common Mode (CM) filter. The novelty of this paper lies in the possibility to fit any equivalent circuit to any impedance curve with a relative efficient algorithm. This allows for back-annotation of fields into equivalent circuit simulators.

articleTitle: 3D coverage optimization research on 5G massive MIMO antenna array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper analyzed the structure of 5G(5th generation mobile system) massive MIMO antenna array, and presented a 3D(three dimension) coverage optimization method. Integrating and optimizing two main plane patterns of the target 3D radiation pattern, the overall 3D beamforming and coverage optimization of the array are realized. In addition, the 3D beamforming optimization method is tested and verified by simulation, which prove the efficiency of optimization method.

articleTitle: A measurement system for passive intermodulation with real time environment parameter detection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A novel method and system for passive intermodulation measurement with real time environment parameter detection is proposed in this thesis. The system includes a high-sensitivity passive intermodulation measurement platform and real-time environmental parameter detection module. Real-time environmental parameter detection module consists of temperature and strain sensors, data acquisition and processing equipment. Precise measurements of temperature and strain are studied to capture the small strains that cause passive intermodulation. Taking rectangular waveguide flange connector as an example, the strain and passive intermodulation under temperature cycling were measured in real time, and the changes of strain and PIM under temperature cycling were obtained.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic analysis of massive vertical interconnects for dense pin assignment optimization using multiple scattering technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A pin assignment evaluation scheme based on electromagnetic multiple scattering techniques is proposed for massively-coupled vertical interconnects in advanced electronic packaging. As the method fully captures the multi-scattering and multi-coupling effects among the cylindrical pins, also called vias, a good characterization of their high-frequency electrical behaviors is obtained up to 100 GHz. The colorful ball-map hot-spot of integrated crosstalk and noise power-sum are presented for design visual aids. Using this evaluation algorithm, the pin assignment of a large package (>70×70 mm) with blocks of cores and input/outputs (>3000 pins) can be accurately simulated and efficiently optimized in a few minutes of computation time.

articleTitle: Active common mode cancellation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces a new way of implementing an Active Common Mode Cancellation filter for removal of common mode signals, generated by inverter dv/dt, in order to reduce conducted emission and bearing currents. it can be applied to all fast switching power applications. This paper focuses on the application case of drive trains for electric or hybrid electric vehicles but the concept is not limited to.

articleTitle: Variability analysis of a boost converter based on an iterative and decoupled circuit implementation of the stochastic Galerkin method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a decoupled and iterative circuit implementation of the stochastic Galerkin method (SGM) for the variability analysis of electrical circuits via polynomial chaos (PC). The method is based on a perturbative reformulation of the SGM, resulting in a decoupled system with equivalent sources that is solved iteratively by suitably updating the sources at each step. This alternative approach is easier to implement and its computational cost scales linearly with the number of unknown PC coefficients. This contribution addresses the case of stochastic resistors. As a validation, the technique is applied to the variability analysis of a boost converter.

articleTitle: EMC design with embedded metamaterial technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Due to the special negative electromagnetic properties, metamaterial has gained wide attention and also been increasingly applied in electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). In the paper, the metamaterial associated EMC design has been addressed through two case studies, one is defected ground structure for common-mode noise inhibition and another is frequency selective surface for the sake of shielding effectiveness for high speed electronics. The results manifest that metamaterial can provide effective solutions to tackle electromagnetic interference issues where conventional EMC approaches are difficult to be deployed or even lose efficacy.

articleTitle: The impact of TID effect on EMS of PDSOI voltage reference circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The paper studies the impact of total ionizing dose (TID) effect on the electromagnetic immunity of voltage reference circuit fabricated with 0.18μm Partial Depletion (PD) Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) CMOS technology. Experiments results show that the output reference voltage of radiation hardened circuit is relatively stable with the dose accumulation up to 300 krad(Si). However, the susceptibility of VSS pin to the high frequency substrate noise deteriorated after irradiation and was partially recovered after 168 hours annealing at room temperature. It can be concluded that for the radiation hardened design of voltage reference, we need to consider not only circuit leakage power and DC electrical characteristics, but also the electromagnetic compatibility of the power supply of the circuit, especially the substrate crosstalk performance.

articleTitle: Statistical eye-diagram estimation method for high-speed channel with N-tap decision feedback equalizer (DFE)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a statistical eye-diagram estimation method for a high-speed channel including N-tap decision feedback equalizer (DFE). This paper proposes a behavior model for the DFE to replace the DFE in the proposed method. The proposed behavior model fully describes the N-tap DFE, which results in successful eye-diagram estimation with the N-tap DFE. In order to show the effect of the DFE depending on its coefficients, this paper shows the corresponding estimated eye-diagrams. For further analysis on the DFE, we also conducted parametric sweep on the coefficient with the proposed method. For verification, we provide a transient simulation under the same condition. From the comparison, the estimated and simulated eye-diagrams are nearly the same. Therefore, this paper successfully proposes and verifies the statistical eye-diagram estimation method with the N-tap DFE for high-speed serial channels.

articleTitle: Eye-diagram estimation with stochastic model for 8B/10B encoded high-speed channel
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes an eye-diagram estimation method for 8B/10B encoded channel. The stochastic model describes the encoder with respect to probability, which replaces the practical encoder. Because the 8B/10B encoder consists of 3-to-4 and 5-to-6 look-up-table (LUTs), they can be represented as its own stochastic model. For verification, we compare the statistical eye-diagram by the proposed method and the SPICE at the same data rate. The changes on the eye-diagram for both cases are nearly the same by the encoder. Therefore, the proposed method successfully achieves the eye-diagram evaluation for the 8B/10B encoded high-speed channel.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic radiation of Xijiang traction substation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation of Xijiang traction substation is studied by metrical, analyses and scientific research, and field strength of power frequency, radio interference and distance attenuation characteristic are acquired in this paper. By scanning frequency in peak detection mode, electrical field and magnetic field strength covering band of 9kHz to 1GHz are obtained, moreover, Quasi-peak measurements at specific frequency points within frequency range are also carried out. In order to reduce influence of high voltage transmission line, a novel “Along Diagonal Extension Line” scheme is proposed and applied in measurement. Measurement results show that field strength around traction substation is less than the emission limit of traction substation, and field strength attenuates with distance increased. Strength of power frequency field is far less than limit of national regulation, in accordance with human's health standard.

articleTitle: High-power broadband honeycomb absorber for 5G millimeter wave chambers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Honeycomb absorber made of Kevlar paper and conductive coating was developed for OTA measurement of 5G phase array antennas. The reflectivity of absorber with thickness about 10 cm can be lower than −40 dB from 18 to 40 GHz, with power handling capability as high as 10 kw/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Current distribution in shielded cable-connector systems for power transmission in electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: With the electrification of vehicle propulsion systems, shielded cables were introduced for delivering the power from HV-battery to inverter and/or from inverter to three-phase motor. On the one hand the shield should improve EMC behaviour, on the other hand the shield should protect passengers and service staff from the high voltage. While in typical communication application of shielded cables the shield carries the return current from the inner conductor and the current sum is zero, the automotive power cable employs a second shielded, and, for three phase applications, a third shielded cable, for the return currents. There is no current injection into the shield. Shield currents are mainly induced by inductive coupling. Knowing the shield currents is essential for evaluating the common mode current and thus the relevant fields caused by a cable configuration. In this paper an analytic approach for estimating the current distribution in and the fields from a shielded cable system for EV for low frequencies is presented. With this method typical systems are calculated and discussed regarding the common mode currents and the magnetic fields.

articleTitle: A possible information leakage from DVI cable corresponding to display color
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the possibility about information leakage from digital visual interface (DVI) cable for color display is analyzed. The principle of information leakage form DVI cable, which already documented before, is reviewed. The electromagnetic emanations from DVI cable are measured for several cases of color display which have different color combination. Also, it is shown that the legibility of recovered image is different with respect to the color combination.

articleTitle: A susceptibility assessment method of high-power electromagnetic effects based on Gaussian process classification and autoregressive co-kriging model
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: High-power electromagnetic (HPEM) environments are capable of causing effects on systems, like malfunctions, performance degradation, interference and even collapse. To research susceptibility of systems under HPEM, experiment is believed as an efficient approach. But for some valuable and complex systems, we have no replacement nor technology to recover faulted system; otherwise, it will cost a heavy price. So we can't perform a lot of experiments and it's hard to collect enough effect data. How to assess susceptibility of systems under HPEM with limited effect data becomes an urgent problem for us. In this paper we introduce a novel statistical method, autoregressive co-kriging model, to deal with this problem. In this model, the real but small experimental data can be merged with rough but big data, such as related state experimental data and experience-based judgment data. Meanwhile, Gaussian process classification (GPC) is used to transform experimental binary data into continuous probability data to fit autoregressive co-kriging model. At the end of this paper, a case study of the susceptibility assessment of a supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system under electromagnetic pulse is illustrated.

articleTitle: Modeling of LEMP propagation in the lossy atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method in the 2D cylindrical coordinate system was used to compute waveforms of nearly full-frequency-bandwidth vertical electric field E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> and azimuthal magnetic field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</sub> produced on the ground surface by lightning return strokes. The conductivity of atmosphere was assumed to increase exponentially with height, with different conductivity profiles being used for daytime and nighttime conditions. The fields were computed at distances ranging from 100 to 500 km. Positive and negative parts of skywaves (reflections from the ionosphere) were identified in computed waveforms and used for estimation of apparent ionospheric reflection heights.

articleTitle: An iterative finite element boundary integral-physical optics method for analyzing shielding effectiveness of a cavity above large platform
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Numerical simulations gain lots of attentions on analyzing shielding effectiveness of electronic equipment. However, most simulations only focus on the equipment itself but neglect the effect of platform, which reduces the reliability of numerical results. For catching the influence of the platform, an iterative finite element boundary integral-physical optics is presented in this paper. Compared with the conventional finite element boundary integral method, the proposed method can efficiently reduce the computational complexity and the number of unknowns. Moreover, to illuminate its validity and efficiency, the proposed method is adopted to analyze the shielding effectiveness of an inhomogeneous cavity above a large platform.

articleTitle: Relay switching at zero-crossing point of grid voltage to eliminate the EFT interference
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A relay application system was proposed to achieve the relay switching exactly at the zero-crossing point of the grid voltage. It can test the delay time between the control signal and relay actual action time under different ambient, assembly positions and load conditions. After consider the delay time of the relay action, the relay can switch exactly at the zero-crossing point of the grid voltage to avoid the grid voltage flicker during the relay action and eliminate one of the fast transient/burst resources in the grid. The operation principle was verified by the prototype and experimental results.

articleTitle: Broadband Green's function with higher order extractions for arbitrary shaped waveguide obeying Neumann boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The broadband Green's function with low wavenumber extraction (BBGFL) consists of low wavenumber method of moments (MoM) solutions combined with modal representations of Green's functions. BBGFL is suitable for broadband simulations because the modal functions are independent of frequencies. In this paper, we extend the formulation of the higher-order extraction method (sixth-order convergence) to an arbitrarily-shaped homogeneous waveguide obeying Neumann boundary conditions. Results from BBGFL are in good agreement with those computed by direct MoM and HFSS. This method can be applied to exact, fast and broadband computation of multiple resonant frequencies and modes of arbitrarily-shaped PCB power/ground planes.

articleTitle: Identification of electromagnetic interferences based on adaptive sparsest time — Frequency analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic interferences measurement system is a multi-input single output system. The signal obtained by the measurement is a mixture of multiple interference signals. In the absence of prior knowledge of the device under test, it is difficult to provide enough support for interference diagnosis and subsequent rectification only using standard measurements in frequency-domain. This paper presents an improved method using adaptive sparse time-frequency analysis (ASTFA) method to achieve the time-domain separation of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) signal. First, the method uses ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) method to decompose the EMI signal into several signal components. Then the average frequency of each component is taken to estimate the initial phase of the ASTFA method to avoid the inaccurate decomposition results caused by the improper guess of initial phase. The proposed method only requires a time-domain measurement of the EMI. A simulation example of the EMI decomposition was given to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of toroidal core for magnetic energy harvester near power line considering saturation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the toroidal core design with improve power density for magnetic energy harvester is proposed. Around the power line, leakage magnetic field is a promising energy source. However, the problem of magnetic saturation can cause power performance degradation of the harvester. To improve power density of magnetic energy harvester, we controlled the inner radius of toroidal core by considering magnetic saturation effect. The proposed idea is validated by theoretical and measurement results.

articleTitle: Investigation of leveling methods in military susceptibility testing: “Leveling under CW signal” and “Leveling under modulated signal”
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Military radiated susceptibility tests performed in accordance with the RS103 section of the MIL-STD461F standard use a 1 kHz, 50% duty cycle pulse modulation during the dwell time in the exposure period of the Device Under Test (DUT). The military standard requires reaching the target field, alias “leveling”, under the modulation unlike its civil counterpart IEC61000-4-3. In other words, in military testing, the modulation must be activated before starting the leveling process and continued during the entire test. On the other hand, the civil radiated susceptibility test performed as per IEC61000-4-3 requires a leveling period under the continuous wave (CW) signal (CW Leveling), thereafter the required modulation (mostly 1 kHz 80% AM) is applied for exposure. Although the military standard stipulates the activation of the modulation before starting the leveling process and its continuation during the entire leveling process, military tests in practice in many laboratories are performed by first using the leveling with the CW signal, afterwards the modulation during the dwell time like the method used in civil applications, for the sake of ease. Furthermore, many test software solutions designed for EMC susceptibility tests employ the same method also for military radiated susceptibility tests as the modulation after the leveling with the CW signal presents an easier and more comfortable test method than the leveling with modulation. Besides, the leveling with the CW signal does not necessitate the use of pulse factors of measurement devices, so that it saves the laboratory from the burden of taking many factors into account. In this research, we investigated the effects of these two leveling methods in detail and emphasized possible differences in test results which may be caused by them. We also used an actual DUT in order to demonstrate that a DUT may fail during the leveling with the CW signal but may pass the test during the dwell time period with modulation which is the actual period desired by the standard to check the DUT for failure. Finally we make some recommendations about the application of military susceptibility testing methods to awaken EMC laboratories to potential pitfalls of the leveling method performed with the CW signal.

articleTitle: Reflective metasurface for generating vortex wave in ultra-wideband
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a metasurface that can generate vortex electromagnetic wave in ultra-wideband is proposed. The metasurface was composed by arrow-shaped elements with different arm lengths in a proper order to covert a plane wave to vortex electromagnetic wave. The simulation results verifies that the reflected wave from the designed reflective metasurface is vortex wave in ultra-wideband from 18GHz to 42GHz, which is in good agreement with the theoretical analysis. The proposed reflective metasurface paves an effective way to generate vortex electromagnetic wave with arbitrary single-mode in ultra-wideband for microwave wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Efficient inductive coupled in-circuit impedance extraction with enhanced SNR and instrument protection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Extraction of in-circuit impedance of an electrical system under its normal operating condition without direct electrical contact has been well-established based on inductively coupling method. This method is useful for noise source impedance extraction of power converter and condition monitoring of critical electrical infrastructures. For in-circuit impedance extraction of high power noisy electrical system, good signal-to-noise ratio and test instrument protection are necessary. This paper proposes a new measurement approach to fulfill such requirements.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impacts of ionospheric scintillation on geosynchronous SAR based on spherical wave correction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) signal influenced by iononspheric scintillation is modeled and analyzed quantitatively based on spherical-wave corrected phase screen simulation. Firstly, the signal traversing and propagting within ionospheric scintillation are modeled and the influences are deduced for point target and area target based on plane wave correction. We find that these models are only suitable for small scene and will surely induce errors in case of larger scenes, especially for GEO SAR. Secondly, the influenced GEO SAR signal model is modified based on the spherical wave corrected phase screen. The impacts of different propagation distance are analyzed. Finally, simulation of area target in large scale is realized based on the proposed method.

articleTitle: A measurement verification for EMI source reconstruction method based on amplitude-only near-field scanning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A modified differential evolution (DE) method is used to reconstruct the equivalent source model of the device under test (DUT) based on amplitude-only near-field scanning in this paper. The equivalent source is a set of infinitesimal magnetic dipoles, which can be used to replace the DUT for electromagnetic interference (EMI) analysis. Then, a test PCB is fabricated to verify this source reconstruction method. The results obtained by the equivalent dipole model have a good agreement with the measured ones.

articleTitle: On the simultaneous switching noise suppression by the integration of Z-shape power bus and bandstop filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: With the development of high technology, the high-speed digital electronic circuit miniaturization, high operating frequency and high-speed transmission of data have continued to improve their functions. Because of the rapid development of semiconductor process, the electronic components become smaller, faster and faster processing speed. Compared to the past electronic circuit systems, the new electronic system will produce unpredictable electromagnetic interference (EMI), signal integrity (Signal Integrity, SI), power integrity (Power Integrity, PI) and other issues. That is to say, Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) has become an important topic in today's design of electronic circuits. Through proposed modelling method, we will discuss High Frequency Suppression Structure with two approaches: the stop-band and pass-band in Z-shape and bandstop filter. In the model, the PCB is divided into five segments of different sizes and rectangular power and ground plane. The High Frequency Suppression Structure are composed of two bandstop filters, rectangular resonant cavity and the Z-shape power bus. Finally, we can effectively isolate the power and ground noise.

articleTitle: Design of an active EMI filter for bearing current elimination in VFD
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: High-frequency currents flow in the bearing of variable frequency induction motors due to parasitic couplings in the motor drive system. An active filter to eliminate the bearing current in a 5 Hp induction motor is simulated in this paper. At higher frequencies, parasitic couplings between stator and rotor windings and the rotor and motor frame are prominent which can cause circulating currents in the bearing when shaft voltage exceeds the breakdown voltage level of the bearing lubricant. This circulating current damages the motor bearing intensely and shortens the life of the motor drastically. Properly designed passive Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) filters can mitigate the high-frequency common-mode voltage across the motor terminals and thus nullify the adverse effects of PWM inverters. However, the components of a passive filter account for a large portion of converter volume, and weight making it expensive. In this paper, an active filter is designed to eliminate the bearing current and to bring down the passive component size.

articleTitle: Analysis of interference caused by intermodulation in multi-tone radiated immunity tests
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, interference caused by intermodulation in multi-tone radiated immunity tests is systematically investigated. The analysis shows that interference of electromagnetic wave will occur when frequencies of multi-tone signals are distributed with arithmetic progression under the condition of three or more frequency signals, which can affect the accuracy of the test results. In order to ensure the quality of the susceptibility test, it must be ensured that power amplifiers are working within their linear operating range. Furthermore, interference can be eliminated when frequencies of any two fundamental signals are not integral multiples of each other and frequencies of any three fundamental signals are not in arithmetic progression distribution.

articleTitle: Probability statistical method of assisting electromagnetic compatibility index decision-making
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The index of equipment and system in the electromagnetic compatibility standards is usually suitable to many kinds of flats, and it is to be right chosen and clip in the actual application based on the engineering practice, or excess design and absent design will bring waste of resource or electromagnetic interference. To the naval ships, it is difficult to carry through accurate modeling adopting traditional numerical simulation method. Recur to probability statistical analysis, we research the rule of electromagnetic emission of potential interferential equipment and sensitive characteristic of potential sensitive equipment, by which forecast the probability of resulting in electromagnetic interference and farther to process analysis and decision-making of equipment and system index. This method on the one hand fully makes use of engineering historical data which have preferable engineering value and directive sense, while on the other hand it avoids abundant numerical modeling which is more simple and feasible.

articleTitle: Effect of contact resistance on conformai shield package for mobile DRAM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In the event of failure to control interference from parts to antennas, the mobile systems cannot perform properly. Also, the EMI certification tests cannot be passed. An effective way to reduce the EMI radiation from components is using a metallic shield can, but it does not meet the demands of miniaturization and flexibility trends in recent mobile devices. A conformal shield package that can compensate for the weakness of shield can is being used more and more. In this paper, the shield effect by applying the conformal shield on package was investigated. For accurate measurement, EMI jig was designed and conformal shield packages were prepared using a silver spray method. Using a near field scan method, the effects of conformal shield packages were investigated. After reducing the contact resistance, the Magnetic field radiation of LP4x was improved by more than 10 dB in all frequency bands. It is founded that the contact resistance management is very critical to ensure uniform EMI characteristics of the conformal shield packages.

articleTitle: New standardized EMC evaluation methods for communication transceivers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces EMC evaluation methods and requirements for communication transceiver ICs described in the new IEC standard series IEC62228. Based on typical results of CAN transceivers, a cross comparison of measurement results on integrated circuit level, component level and vehicle level will be provided. The correlation of results and the potential to harmonize requirements in respect to test methods and effort will be discussed.

articleTitle: Principle and electromagnetic immunity of ADAS millimeter — Wave radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Intelligent vehicles use millimeter-wave radar as environment-aware sensors to achieve driver assistant functions. The electromagnetic immunity tolerance of the millimeter-wave radar system will affect the realization of driver assistant function and driving safety. Based on the study of the principle and target recognition theory of the millimeter-wave radar system, the millimeter-wave radar system is activated by target simulating method, and the electromagnetic immunity test of the millimeter-wave radar system is carried out under different field strengths. The experimental results show that the millimeter-wave radar system could be disturbed by the external electromagnetic signal under certain field strength, and serious malfunction occurs. Through the systematic research, technical support can be provided to the enterprise R&D test and technical skills and experiences are prepared for the formulation of the test specifications or standards.

articleTitle: Placement of decoupling capacitors on power transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A method is proposed for efficient placement of decoupling capacitor on a power transmission line based on calculating the critical distance between device power pin and the capacitor. The critical distance is measured from the power pin and refers to the spacing for which the capacitor's effectiveness is reduced by a predefined amount with respect to the power pin. The resulting transcendental equation is solved for the distance using an iterative approach. The proposed method is validated by comparing to full wave electromagnetic simulation results.

articleTitle: Most energy-efficient input voltage function for RC delay line
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents the most energy-efficient input voltage function for RC delay line. The Euler-Lagrange's differential equation for the circuit is derived thoroughly. General solution of the differential equation is presented. However, determining the unique solution leads to an ill-conditioned problem easily. Here, a solution of the ill-conditioned problem is proposed. The general solution is manipulated in a form in terms of hyperbolic sine functions, a linear function and a constant. Using this form, the ill-conditioned problem can be alleviated with the condition numbers improved. Then, the unique solution is determined. The lowest energy dissipation and the lowest input energy are derived analytically. Finally, the energy dissipation of the most energy-efficient input voltage function is compared with ramp function for various final time.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling analysis of multiple on-board antennas with sub-domain MoM-PO method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The sub-domain (SD) method of moments (MoM) is hybridized with the physical optics (PO) to efficiently handle multiple on-board antennas. Each antenna is assigned as one subdomain and simulated with the MoM separately, and interactions between subdomains are taken into account with proper boundary conditions and an iterative procedure. Not only memory usage is reduced, but also each subdomain can be discretized independently. To analyze the mutual coupling between on-board antennas, we derive the formulations through the equivalent multi-port network concepts. Numerical results show good accuracy of the SD-MoM-PO method.

articleTitle: Fast evaluation of low frequency near field magnetic shielding effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a fast approach is presented for the evaluation of near field magnetic shielding effectiveness. Generally, in the literature the near field shielding is determined from far field formulas while modifying the wave impedance. The paper shows that adding a corrective term in the generic expression of the shielding effectiveness allows predicting accurately the shielding when the source of disturbance is a magnetic dipole. In order to deduce shielding effectiveness in practical cases the approach presented in this paper relies in two steps. The first replace the real source of disturbances with a set of equivalent magnetic dipoles. In the second step the shielding effectiveness is determined with the dipoles as actual sources and using improved expressions including the corrective term. The modeling methodology is validated experimentally in case of a radiating coil located near a conducting planer shield.

articleTitle: A low-profile dual-band-pass FSS applied to Wi-Fi communication systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we design a low-profile FSS for Wi-Fi communication with two bands, i.e. 2.4-GHz and 5.5-GHz. The FSS incorporates the two traditional FSS units, the Jerusalem cross (the J-cross) and nested loops, showing a good performance in terms of the bandstop and insensitivity to angles of the incident wave. In addition, the single-unit-based FSSs with either the J-cross or nested loops are studied, verifying the mutual coupling between the J-cross and loops in our design which can decrease the resonant frequency and excite the dual-resonant-frequency. Finally, the current distributions at 2.4 GHz and 5.5 GHz with varying polarizations and angles of the incident wave are investigated thoroughly, and then reasons for the shifts of resonant frequencies with polarizations and angles are given.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic coupling effects of spacecraft solar panel
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Seldom protective measures are adopted in the installation of spacecraft solar panel power lines, which leaves hidden trouble to the coupling of interference signals. In this paper, the mechanisms of transient electromagnetic field and continuous electromagnetic field coupled with the solar panel power lines to emit radiation in the spacecraft cabin and then interfere with the low voltage differential signaling (LVDS) communication bus are studied. The experiments verify that the solar panel power line is indeed a strong electromagnetic energy coupling channel. The interference frequencies of the solar panel power line and the sensitive threshold of the LVDS bus are determined, meanwhile the experimental results are verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Broadband lumped circuit parameter extraction method based on PEEC
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a precise, concise and physical lumped circuit parameter extraction method to build a broadband effective circuit model for a passive component or an interconnector based on PEEC theory. The external port impedance matrix is firstly built up by multiplying the selector matrix and the branch voltage matrix root from n+1 nodes PEEC network. Then, a polynomial form of the port impedance matrix is obtained using generalized eigenvalue theory. The reduced order circuit model can be obtained by removing high frequency terms and the reduced order circuit parameters can be calculated by matrix transform too. Spiral PCB planar inductor's circuit parameters are extracted using the method proposed and the simulation and test results prove the reduced order model is effective till 700MHz.

articleTitle: ICIM-CPI: Integrated circuits immunity model: Conducted pulse immunity: Description, extraction and example
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The Integrated circuits immunity model-Conducted pulse immunity (ICIM-CPI) has been developed to allow the simulation of the conducted transient immunity of an Integrated Circuit (IC) to pulses such as Electrostatic discharge (ESD) and Electric fast transient (EFT). The model, in its current form, addresses voltage breakdown and thermal breakdown failures. The model is intended to be used for predicting the immunity levels to conducted pulses disturbances applied on IC pins. It is intended to be used for predicting the immunity level, both damage and function failure, to conducted pulses disturbances applied on IC pins.

articleTitle: 45-Degree polarized microstrip grid arrays for millimeter-wave micro base station
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Micro base stations will play an important role in the future millimeter-wave mobile networks. This paper presents a new array design for millimeter-wave micro base stations. The array is a microstrip grid structure configured to radiate 45-degree polarized waves. It was implemented in a low-cost FR4 PCB technology and tested in the 28-GHz band. It is shown that the array with a size of 20×20×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> achieved the wide bandwidth of more than 28% and high gain of 11.4 dBi at 28.5 GHz. More importantly, it is found that the performance of the array is insensitive to the location at and size of the grounded substrate and there is a large isolation between ± 45-degree polarized arrays, indicating its suitability to micro base stations of various sizes and dual polarizations.

articleTitle: 1 to 4 Way wideband power divider using substrate integrated waveguide and modified Wilkinson structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, 1 to 4 way wideband power divider using substrate integrated waveguide and modified Wilkinson structures are presented. Two stages of a 2-way power divider and their arrangement to form a 4-way power divider for feeding the input perpendicular to the substrate are discussed. The simulated transmission coefficients, reflection coefficients and isolation for the 2-way power dividers and the 4-way power dividers are also discussed. The designed 4-way power divider with substrate integrated waveguide and modified Wilkinson has a -10 dB impedance from 1.6 GHz to 3.5 GHz having a fractional bandwidth of 74.5%.

articleTitle: Modeling of EMP coupling to lossless MTLs in time domain based on analytical Gauss-Seidel iteration technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper provides an efficient way to simulate the transient electromagnetic field coupling to overhead multi-conductor transmission lines in time domain based on an analytical iterative technique. The method is entirely in time domain and therefore can handle straightforwardly nonlinear loads. In this method, the interaction between the line conductors are represented by distributed sources, and the time domain analytical expressions of the transient response along transmission lines are derived step by step by adopting the waveform relaxation and Gauss-Seidel iteration techniques. The efficiency of the proposed method for both linear and nonlinear loads is demonstrated through validation examples. The numerical performance of the method, in terms of accuracy and CPU time, are found to be superior to that of conventional FDTD method. Furthermore, the proposed method allows to obtain similar accuracy as in FDTD with considerably larger time steps. The method is therefore very efficient for evaluating the transient response of long overhead multi-conductor transmission lines illuminated by external electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: A high-gain circularly-polarized patch antenna design using an advanced shielding technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain circularly-polarized antenna is created by integrating a simple linearly-polarized patch antenna and an advanced electromagnetic shielding. This shielding is specially designed to have a band-pass property which could reduce the electromagnetic interference (EMI) of the shielded system and allow its signal wave radiated from the internal antenna to pass through. Moreover, the shielding could transform a linearly-polarized wave to circularly-polarized and highly increase its gain as well.

articleTitle: Analytical calculation of transformer parameters by S-parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper proposed a new methodology and dedicated algorithm to extract the parameters of transformer from S-parameters by Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) measurement. Analytical expressions of S parameters are deduced for each transformer parameter including basic and parasitic parameters based on the interconnection and transformation theory between Y/ABCD/S parameters of the optimized equivalent circuit of transformer. The analytical calculation is also verified by circuit simulation with high accuracy (<;0.6% deviation).

articleTitle: Improved efficiency characteristics of wireless power charging system for superconducting MAGLEV train using inserted permanent magnets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: As the wireless power transfer (WPT) technology based on strongly resonance coupled method realizes large power charging without any wires through the air, there are advantages compared with the wired counterparts, such as convenient, safety and fearless transmission of power. From this reason, the WPT systems have started to be applied to the wireless charging for various power applications such as transportations (train, underwater ship, electric vehicle). This study aims for the design and analysis of antenna and receiver with high efficiency and stability in wireless power charging system for superconducting magnetic levitation (MAGLEV) train. Authors have already been developed superconducting wireless power charging (WPC) system for MAGLEV train using resonance copper antenna (Tx) coil HTS receiver (Rx) coil. Since the Tx and Rx coils can be placed on guidance and superconducting magnet at train, respectively, the installation cost of Tx can be considerably reduced. In this study, authors described and compared the practical design of permanent magnet between copper Tx and HTS Rx coils to improve the transfer efficiency through rectifying module since the permanent magnets can play a role to shift the transferred AC magnetic field. Authors measured rectifying currents under inserted permanent magnets with radio frequency (RF) power of 370 kHz below 150 W.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic environment threat level requirement for military aircraft susceptibility testing in support of high intensity radiated field qualification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The UK have a requirement to establish Electromagnetic Environment (EME) threat levels, covering the frequency range 790 MHz to 50 GHz, on which to base investment in a radiated susceptibility Electromagnetic Environmental Effects (E3) High Intensity Radiated Field (HIRF) test system for military aircraft. Numerous international standards specifying EMEs were initially reviewed but were found to differ significantly in terms of stated EME magnitudes. In addition, they did not address the parameters of Pulse Width (PW), Pulse Repetition Frequency (PRF) and Duty Cycle (DC), which are considered important for avionic system testing, because such data is often classified.
