The resulting assessment presented in this paper combines both a review of the EMEs, based on established UK and international standards, with a detailed assessment of world-wide threat transmission parameters in order to address the PW, PRF and DC parameters. Assessing the threat parameters includes addressing near and far-field electromagnetic propagation from microwave transmission antennas. Finally, the required parameters for the HIRF EME are declared.

articleTitle: Analysis on the adaptability of the international radiation immunity test method to intelligent connected vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This article analyzes the main sensitive equipment and frequency characteristics of intelligent connected vehicle in the near future, theoretical analysis and simulation analysis of the antenna method and the TLS method is carried out for the adaptability of international vehicle radiation immunity, and actual electric field distribution in vehicle is evaluated. The author puts forward the shortcomings of the international radiation immunity certification test in the adaptability of intelligent connected vehicle, and proposes an improved methods according to the analysis results.

articleTitle: Estimation and analysis of crosstalk effects in high-bandwidth memory channel
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In This paper, we present an efficient crosstalk-included eye-diagram estimation with simulation and measurement results. Crosstalk level, total jitter, and eye height are analyzed from the obtained eye-diagram. Crosstalk effects show substantial impact on eye-diagram in HBM channel.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic interference investigation of PCB in metallic enclosures using ADI-FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, transient electromagnetic analysis of rectangular metallic enclosures with apertures illuminated by electromagnetic pulse (EMP) is investigated using alternating-direction-implicit finite-difference time-domain (ADI-FDTD) method. The dispersive property of substrate of printed circuits boards (PCBs) is characterized by the Debye model. Numerical results shows that induced voltage of inner circuits are seriously affected by angle of incidence, polarization and magnitude of the EMP, and length of apertures. Based on the transient response, further design of protection can be implemented to suppress the received jitter of voltage pulses.

articleTitle: Performance improvement for sub-nanosecond Marx generator based on avalanche transistors by considering the traveling wave process
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The Marx generator is an important device in pulse power technology for generating high voltage pulses. In general, the equivalent circuit of Marx generator circuit is a lumped parameter circuit under the condition of electrically small. However, for a Marx generator generating very short pulses such as ultra-wideband pulses, it is necessary to consider the wave process of pulse forming from the original terminal to the output terminal. In this paper, the circuit model of Marx generator involved distributed transmission lines is introduced, which considering the wave process. The difference between the newly raised Marx generator circuit model and the traditional Marx circuit is demonstrated by simulation and experiment. Based on this circuit model, it is useful to explain the pulse forming process accurately and to optimize the pulser design.

articleTitle: Mathematic subarray decomposition to compose the radiation of electrically large phased array of antennas with limited excitation power in measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a strategy to measure the radiation from an electrically large phased array of antennas with high-power excitations. The motivation arises from the insufficient power supply and safety requirement in the measurement system. We propose the decomposition of the original array into mathematically overlapped arrays each with locally emphasized excitations to fulfill the safety requirement of radiation inside a chamber. The radiations of these decomposed arrays may also serve as the field basis functions to calibrate the radiation patterns of the original array with sufficiently reduced time. Both numerical simulations and experimental measurements are shown to demonstrate the validity.

articleTitle: Analyzing the model of transformer windings under very fast transient overvoltage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The Very Fast Transient Overvoltage (VFTO) can produce electromagnetic interference and influence the secondary equipment greatly in conventional substation. To analyze the influence of VFTO in secondary equipment in transformers, this article introduces the multiconductor transmission lines model (MTL) and derives the transfer function of parallel-interleaved of transformer windings. At the last of the article, Simulink and physical experiments are carried out to verify the correctness of this method.

articleTitle: The Associated Hermite FDTD method: Developments and applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper briefly reviewed the developments and applications of the unconditionally stable finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method based on the Associated Hermite (AH) orthogonal functions-AH FDTD method. It is a time domain tool but shares with some similar performance with FDFD (finite-difference frequency-domain) method. In addition, it can also be represented as a bridge of FDTD and FDFD method, which especially has advantages for efficiently solving frequency-dependent problems in time domain.

articleTitle: An introduction to MIMO antenna array designs for future 5G smartphone applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this Talk, various MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) antenna array designs for future 5G smartphone applications working in the Sub-6GHz bands (LTE band 42 and band 43) will be introduced. A short introductory on the differences between Sub-6GHz band and mmWave band on future 5G technology will also be mentioned. The theory, methodology, and further experimental results of these reported antennas will be discussed further during the session presentation.

articleTitle: HT-detection method based on impedance measurements of ICs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Threats that cause information leakage by adding Hardware Trojan (HT) to a device constructed using inexpensive elements after shipment have been reported. In this paper, we focus on the HT implemented in the wiring connected to integrated circuits (ICs). We propose a detection method for such HT implemented outside the IC by measuring the change in the impedance of the wiring.

articleTitle: Study on the searching strategies of assessing the MRI RF-induced heating for an implantable plate and screw system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison study of searching strategies for the worst-case construct for an implantable internal fixation system under 1.5T MRI radio frequency (RF) birdcage coil. An example of the generic plate and screw system is used as the device of interest. Based on the combinations of the values of the six device parameters, 576 models are studied and the peak 1 g averaged specific absorption rate (SAR) near devices are extracted to build a dataset for searching. Three searching strategies, which are sequential one-dimension searching, searching based on various sequences and searching with multi-iterations, are investigated. It is found that the searching sequences and initial values of the device parameters have effects on the searched worst-case results. The possibility of getting the failed search results when searching with random sequence and initial parameter values can be high. Searching with multi-iterations can improve the accuracy of correctly identifying the worst-case heating construct.

articleTitle: Research on the influence of metal groove on wires coupling in EMU
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: More metal grooves were used in EMU to neatly arrange the wires. On one hand, they protect wires against external electromagnetic interference and reduce external radiation from the wires. On the other hand, the metal grooves create waveguide structures that affect the coupling among wires inside the metal grooves. To study the influence of the metal groove's different parameters on the coupling between wires, an equivalent metal groove model was established in this paper. In the equivalent model, it is very convenient to change the parameters of the metal groove. By changing these parameters, the results of wires coupling in a variety of cases that is not easy to realize in reality can be obtained. The results can provide an effective reference for the design of metal grooves. The equivalent model was validated by measurements.

articleTitle: Resonator approach for simple calculation of total microwave energy accumulated inside the shielding box
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Involving the theory of microwave resonators total energy of microwave radiation passing through the metal screen of electronic devices is under investigation. Two main types of electromagnetic waves excitation in shielded volume at the resonant frequencies are considered including a narrow slit and wired connections. The slit length was found to be main factor in total energy dependence in resonant manner rather then its width. Same dependence between total energy and length of external wiring is identified. According to calculations, microwave energy at shield resonant frequencies can exceed several micro joules that can be destructive for a number of sensitive electronic components.

articleTitle: The insertion loss calculation research of multiple filters in series and parallel connection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: With the development of power electronics technique, more and more high-power electronics devices are applied in the power system. EMI filters are spread used to reduce the electromagnetic interference generated by these devices. But it is very difficult to manufacture high-voltage filter capacitors and heavy-current filter inductors. Several low-power filters can be connected in series or in parallel to realize a high-power filter. The insertion loss calculation method of such filter is researched in this paper. First, the relationship between the insertion loss (IL) and the two-port network parameters has been derived. Then the insertion loss of multiple filters connected in series and in parallel is researched by experiments. Finally, two filters connected in parallel were designed for a high-power inverter. The measurement results verified the validity of the theoretical derivation.

articleTitle: An integrated UHF/UWB tag antenna with radome for indoor positioning system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In practical scenario, the RFID tag antenna should be encapsulated into a relative close environment for protecting from physical and electromagnetic interference (EMI) damage. However, the presence of radome will, in general, affect the matching and radiation characteristics of antennas due to the induced displacement current on the radome. In this paper, we model the radome and investigate its influence to antenna performance though simulation. The employed antenna is a miniaturized dual-band antenna, with an overall size of only 52.7 mm (length) × 50 mm (width) × 5 mm (profile). The impedance bandwidth can handle 920 MHz to 925 MHz (UHF) and 3.0 GHz to 5.14 GHz (UWB), with stable gain for the specified indoor positioning systems. A compact radome is fabricated with 3D printing technology and its influence is experimentally verified with integrated RF circuits.

articleTitle: Method of data acquisition and map generation for radio frequency electromagnetic fields exposure level
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper provides guidance on how to acquire data and make radio-frequency electromagnetic field (RF-EMF) maps for assessing existing exposure levels over large areas of cities or territories and for an appropriate public disclosure of the results, in a simple and understandable way. It describes the methods and tools for the development of the RF-EMF maps and gives an example of map-making.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-thermal simulation of Lorentz media by the DGTD method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the transient electromagnetic-thermal simulation via the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method is performed for the Lorentz medium, which is a kind of dispersive material with frequency-dependent permittivity. To avoid doing the convolution in the time domain, the auxiliary differential equation (ADE) method is adopted to manipulate the dispersive relation. The transient dielectric loss of Lorentz media is derived according to the electrodynamic approach and is treated as the heat source for transient thermal simulation. The accuracy and validity of the proposed method are demonstrated by the numerical example.

articleTitle: Solution to range and velocity ambiguities based on frequency diversity MIMO radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The colocated multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar can simultaneously obtain the multi-dimensional information of target for its diversity advantage. Combining the idea of MIMO radar and multiple pulse repetition frequency (PRF), this paper uses multiple orthogonal signals with different medium PRF simultaneously to obtain the target's range and velocity information of different PRF through matched filtering at the receiver. In the simulations, four orthogonal signals at four different PRF are transmitted to obtain the range and velocity information from the total echo signal. All of the results show the feasibility of this model.

articleTitle: Efficient analysis of switching noise suppression of SMPS boards using segmentation method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a design technique based on segmentation method for efficient simulation of common-mode switching noise suppression in switched-mode power supply printed circuit boards (SMPS PCBs). Using a proposed method, a simulation time is substantially reduced up to 46 %, thus achieving an efficient simulation.

articleTitle: A LPDA free-space factor calibration
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The free space antenna factor to measure the emission noise from EUT is specified in the international standard. The free space factor was also specified with transition to VCCI - CISPR32 in Japan. The calibration method of free space factor for Biconical Antenna is described on ANSI C63.5-2017Annex G with apply correction value of table G1 to the near free space factor. On the other hand, for Log-Periodical Dipole Array (LPDA), the correction value is not shown in the standard, and it is described that the factor in near free space may be used as it is. And also averaging method is describing in CISPR 16-1-6 but this method normally required about 10m height antenna mast. From above reason, the calibration laboratory is limited here in Japan. From those reason, VCCI technical subcommittee (working group of Antenna calibration and site evaluation) decided to compare the calibratedfree space factor with near free space factor of LPDA.

articleTitle: Embedded multilayer interleaved comb capacitor for package-level EMI protection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a new embedded multilayer interleaved comb (MIC) capacitor structure for package level and on-chip level electromagnetic interference (EMI) protection. The proposed structure can be implemented using multiple metal layers available in package and on-chip. In comparison with the traditional on-chip capacitor using metal planes, the proposed MIC capacitor has higher capacitance density by as much as 60%, while the parasitic resistance and inductance are lower. The mathematical models are developed to estimate the capacitance, parasitic inductance and resistance of MIC capacitor structure are presented. To validate the model, 3D field solver is used and a prototype of MIC capacitor is manufactured using the interconnect layers of 180nm CMOS process and the characteristics are measured.

articleTitle: A horizontally polarized omnidirectional millimeter wave microstrip antenna with miniaturized dual-bent-“S”-shaped structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Based on the Alford loop structure, this paper is focused on a miniaturized design of horizontally polarized omnidirectional millimeter wave microstrip antenna for the usage of the future mobile communication systems. 28 GHz is one of the most potential and leading band for the upcoming 5G, and here is selected as the center working frequency of our antenna design. The proposed antenna can provide an omnidirectional radiation pattern in horizontal plane, through the structural design of smoothing the current distributions on the whole radiated loop strip. The whole “leaf” like loop is composed by four equal bent strips, where each two opposite ones are the two wings of the defined “S”-shaped structures on the both sides of our designed microstrip antenna. Furthermore, there is a bent design on each wing to realize the structure miniaturization. In simulation, we can get an effective working bandwidth of around 460 MHz (27.91-28.37 GHz) with the reflection coefficient |5ii| of lower than -10 dB. Besides, in order to do the verification easily, the proposed antenna is scaled up to the size working at the center frequency of 2.4S GHz, the simulated and measured results of which coincide with each other.

articleTitle: Challenges of multi-scale modelling for system-level EMI simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: As telecom equipments evolving toward higher frequency and higher speed, system-level EMI problems become more and more prominent in high frequency. Usually, high speed digital ICs, connectors and PCBs are the most important components in a ICT product, and at the same time, the most complicated and challenging parts for EMI modeling when system level EMI simulation to be performed. In this paper, an equivalent modeling method to solve such problems was investigated and proposed. Through near-field test and modeling, Multi-link superimposition for connector radiation, PCB ACS equivalent modeling, etc., the complexity of modeling such complicated components in big systems is simplified to a large extent and thereby, the accuracy of system-level EMI risk assessment through simulation been greatly improved.

articleTitle: A novel dual channel receive front-end module with MEMS technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces an dual channel receive front-end module which is fabricated by MEMS package technology. The module is composed of radio frequency (RF) components, is extremely-small, low-cost and high reliability. The microwave monolithic integrated circuits of the receive front-end module are mounted onto a silicon substrate fabricated by the MEMS technology. Some passive components, such as the filters, the attenuators and the transmission lines, are embedded in the silicon substrate. The full module consists of two low noise amplifiers, two digital attenuators, two mixers, a power divider, some chip capacitances and two MEMS filters. The measured receive gain and the output power at 1-dB gain compression point are 5dB and 0dBm respectively. By comparing with the samples obtained by the common process, while the performance of them are basically the same, which verifies the feasibility of the technical approach.

articleTitle: The interconnected wireless world, a major challenge for EM-coexistence
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The number of wireless devices is growing rapidly, and are also deployed in many environments, which is posing new challenges for EMC engineers. This paper discusses the trends and impact, and describes the Electro-Magnetic Diversity as a concept for achieving EM coexistence. The reason for publishing, and the impact of, the new European Radio equipment Directive is discussed. Generic measures to achieve the EM Compatibility, i.e. the required selectivity and low unwanted emission, are given.

articleTitle: Modal analysis of reflection of TDR in overhead distribution lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Detection of a fault point in an overhead distribution system is necessary for accident restoration in power grid. Applying a pulse wave to the overhead distribution line and measurement of reflection wave, which is called TDR measurement with utility-pole-interval resolution, can detect distance to the fault point. In this report, an overhead distribution line is treated as a three-conductor transmission line with earth ground. Eigen modes in the transmission line are derived by inductances and capacitance matrices calculated by electrostatic or magnetostatic simulator. In addition, a fundamental matrix of an equivalent circuit model of a fault point is expressed by impedances and admittances. The fundamental matrix is converted to a modal S parameter. Reflection coefficient with mode conversion of disconnection fault case is calculated using derived S parameter. The calculated reflection coefficients are in good agreement with calculation results using a circuit simulator. As a results, considering mode conversion in the TDR method can detect type of fault in the overhead distribution lines.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic resonance analysis of a shielding enclosure with apertures excited by a plane wave
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic resonances in a shielding enclosure with apertures could cause significant degradation of its shielding performance. In this paper, the resonance properties of a shielding enclosure with apertures excite by a plane wave are analyzed based on the Bethe's theory for small apertures and waveguide theory. The transmitted fields through each aperture are equivalent to fields radiated by a magnetic current located at the center of the aperture. The resonant modes and resonant frequencies of the enclosure are determined according to the direction of the magnetic current and the radiated fields. The results are verified by full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Comparison test and error analysis of the TEM cell method in IC radiated emission
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic emission measurement aims to provide the level of conducted or radiated emission produced by a device under test (DUT) in a given configuration. The risk of the DUT interfering with the limits defined by a standard or customers, then the DUT is either declared EMC compliance or not. The IEC 61967-2 standard defines a method for measuring the electromagnetic radiation from an integrated circuit (IC). The comparison test was performed in three electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing laboratories. Verify the test equipment, test sites, test methods on the test results. Possible causes for variations in emissions with the different systems are discussed, and some improvement measures and precautions have been provided.

articleTitle: A joint method of EMT and DEMATEL in analyzing HEMP coupling effect of phased array radar antenna system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In the protection of phased array radar against HEPM, a joint method of EMT(electromagnetic topology) and DEMATEL is proposed to reduce the difficulty of determining the coupling path. The phased array radar, whose structure and electrical equipment is complicated to meet its function, is decomposed into several subsystem using electromagnetic topology so that it can be simulated separately by full wave method. DEMATEL method is used to analyze the topology network and identify the factor that contributes most to the system coupling effect. And then the weak path can be obtained immediately by connecting those factor in series. Compared to the traditional graph theory solution, the proposed method simplified the process significantly and possesses better efficiency.

articleTitle: Effect of conducting surfaces on the performance of common mode chokes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this work we use a high-frequency circuit model of a common mode choke to study the effect of conducting structures made of copper tape on the attenuation provided by the common mode choke. We analyze the effect on the attenuation of common mode and differential mode noise of grounded and ungrounded conducting surfaces placed near a stand-alone common mode choke. We also analyze the effect on a EMI filter. The main aim is to determine whether the response of the common mode choke can be modified and to identify and quantify the physical mechanism responsible for the change in the response of the EMI filter. This study allows us to devise an optimum shield for a common mode choke that can improve the attenuation to both the common mode and the differential noise of an EMI filter at high frequencies, where parasitics usually undermine the performance of the filter. Key features of this technique are that it can be applied on-site and that it does not result in increase of the weight, volume or cost of the filter.

articleTitle: Efficient analysis of ESD noise coupling to mobile device memory module
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This study presents an efficient way for the estimation of the induced electrostatic discharge (ESD) noise to mobile device memory modules in circuit simulation environment. The induced noise due to ESD event at the commercial laptop dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) modules is calculated using the coupling transfer impedance function in SPICE type circuit simulator. Coupling transfer function is derived from the measured S-parameters using proposed novel method. The comparison of measured and circuit simulated results using coupling transfer impedance function shows very good agreement.

articleTitle: Parametric study of impact of static magnetic field on human cell viability
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper provides a parametric study of a static magnetic field (SMF) to the cell viability. Four types of human cells were selected for exposure to SMF with different durations and levels of intensity in our experiment. The cell viability was investigated by comparing the viable cell count with the control groups; flow cytometry was adopted for cell apoptosis test in our experiment. An intensity of 0.25mT, 0.5mT, and 1mT exposure with 24 hours, 48 hours and 72 hours were examined for chronical low level static field exposure. The outcome of the experiment has indicated that the SMF can influence the rate of cell viability. It is concluded that there is no significant variation for the 0.25mT and 0.5mT, while at 1mT the cell apoptosis is obvious with a p-value of less than 0.05 at a confidence interval of 95%. Our multivariable parametric study was confirmed by linear regression analysis in Stata.

articleTitle: Efficient electromagnetic simulation of PCB with SPICE elements by using HIE-FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: The HIE-FDTD method is one of the fast electromagnetic simulation techniques. The HIE-FDTD method has been extended to perform the electromagnetic simulation including the linear/nonlinear elements. However, this extension does not perform the electromagnetic simulation including the complex circuit models. This paper describes the HIE-FDTD method with circuit simulator for the efficient electromagnetic simulation with the SPICE elements.

articleTitle: Fault state behavior of smart power devices during electromagnetic interference
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper the robustness of smart power ICs to electromagnetic interferences (EMI) coupled into their supply and output pins will be shown. In particular, the susceptibility of the integrated protection and diagnosis functionality will be investigated. It will be shown to what extent such devices can correctly detect fault conditions to ensure functional safety, robustness and reliability tasks, if electromagnetic interferences are coupled into their pins.

articleTitle: On the evaluation of electromagnetic information leakage from mobile device screens
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: We present a statistical testing based methodology for evaluating electromagnetic radiation from a tested mobile device that potentially contains exploitable information for re-constructing screen images of the device. The basic idea is to employ a statistical test instead of reconstructing screen images. The validity of our methodology is demonstrated in a real-world setting by an experiment observing EM radiation from a tablet device's screen that would be usable in a TEMPEST attack.

articleTitle: Influence of mutual coupling on parasitic capacitance in common mode chokes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In the search for a physics based model for a Common Mode Choke (CMC), the high frequency behavior of a multitude of chokes is studied. The high frequency behavior (above self-resonance) is often regarded as purely capacitive, while actually/obviously it has an inductive origin as well. The goal of this paper is to highlight and characterize this behavior and to warn for a common misconception.

articleTitle: Extension of signal-to-noise ratio measurement method to byte-by-byte side-channel attack
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of side-channel traces leaked from cryptographic ICs can be a candidate of system-designer-friendly design index in security evaluation against the side-channel attack (SCA). A method to calculate SNR of side-channel traces from measured side-channel traces was proposed for the scenario of the byte-by-byte attack on AES cryptographic circuits. The proposed method was a simple extension of an SNR calculation method for the brute force attack scenario proposed in a previous study. Measured SNRs according to the methods were validated by comparison with analytical formulas. Results suggested that the proposed method could provide SNRs of side-channel traces accurately.

articleTitle: Invasive weed optimized planar elliptical dipole antenna for ultra-wideband EMC applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for optimizing a planar elliptical dipole antenna for ultra-wideband EMC applications. The Invasive Weed optimization (IWO) method is used, which is a nature inspired metaheuristic evolutionary algorithm. The goal is to achieve maximum boresight realized gain and minimum reflection coefficient S11 across the frequency range of 1 GHz to 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Smart metasurface with non-reciprocity for Fog layer in IoT environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Recent rapid advancement of wireless communication prevails wireless user terminals by high density in space. This spread of wireless equipments leads to high congestion of electromagnetic environment, therefore innovative metasurface working as “electromagnetic field coordinator” is immensely desirable in order to support highly reliable communication. In this paper, a smart metasurface with non-reciprocity for fog layer in IoT environment is proposed and prototype implementation by slot-ring resonator with switchable FET isolator is examined as a proof of concept. The presented structure exhibits full transmission control feature by external applied bias voltage to FET. This type of smart metasurface implementation can provide stable and reliable IoT communication environment.

articleTitle: Introduction to EM information security for IoT devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: With the advent of the Internet of Things (IoT), many electronic devices (e.g., smart meters, surveillance cameras, mobile devices, and multiple sensors) are interconnected. Each device gathers data and uploads it to servers via communication networks. Servers store the large volumes of received data in databases. Applications analyze this data and extract valuable information. Finally, based on this information, new services (in domains such as smart cities, public safety, e-commerce, medical, healthcare, or automobile) are provided. In this data flow, systems and applications in the upper layer trust the hardware in the lower layer, which includes data-gathering devices. If the collected information is intentionally modified by adversaries, services in the upper layer could be disrupted. Therefore, to ensure service continuity in the IoT, it is important to secure the hardware layer in which data are harvested and transmitted. In this paper, we focus on hardware-level security in IoT systems and classify the schemes proposed for physical security of IoT into three categories. We also provide examples for each of these and explain threats and countermeasures.

articleTitle: Finite-difference time-domain method for multilayer carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer panel using tensorial conductivity matrix
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method for multilayer carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) panel using tensorial conductivity matrix. By proper interpolation, all the electromagnetic field components involved in the FDTD update equations are all located in the Yee's cell in a staggered manner. Based on the measured tensorial conductivity matrix, the anisotropic characteristic of multilayer CFRP panel with different fiber orientations in different layers is modeled. A unidirectional CFRP panel is simulated to show the current density distributions for different tensorial conductivity matrice. In addition, a lightning-like source striking at an infinite large multilayer multidirectional CFRP panel truncated by convolutional perfectly matched layer (CPML) is also simulated. The current densities and the electric fields at the center point for the top four layers testify the conductive loss along the in-depth direction.

articleTitle: Electrical-thermal co-simulation for through silicon via and active tier in 3-D IC
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: An electrical-thermal co-simulation method for through silicon via (TSV) and active tier in 3-D IC is presented in this paper. Based on the thermal-electrical analogy, both steady and transient co-simulation can be performed in frequently-used circuit solver. Accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method are demonstrated by numerical examples, which also show that active tiers have a greater effect on the whole thermal performance.

articleTitle: Ceramic interconnect bridge for heterogeneous multiple chip packaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we describe the architecture and performance of a fine pitch multiple chip heterogeneous integration solution using ceramic interconnect bridge on organic substrate package. We present the increased IO density and improvement of electrical high-speed performance on signal integrity are achievable through this novel chiplets integration scheme, where dense copper routings on small ceramic bridges are served as electrical interconnect. The cost and signal attenuation of using ceramic bridge is far better than that of a silicon bridge or a wafer interposer on substrate.

articleTitle: Impacts to measurement uncertainty of radiated EMI measurement by setting terminating condition of AC mains cable leaving from test area
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This paper verifies the degree of influence that the standardization of mains cable termination condition which is currently proposed with CISPR/SC-I gives to the Standards Compliance Uncertainty (SCU). First of all, we presumed the uncertainty value of the mains cable termination in the radiating emission measurement from the results of Round Robin Test which circulated the same EUT, the same cable termination device, and the same mains cable layout. And then, the radiating emission levels which were calculated considering with the tolerance of the termination impedance were used for presuming the measurement uncertainty when the mains cable was terminated by the device. Finally, the expanded Measurement Instrumentation Uncertainty (MIU) including the uncertainty by AC mains cable terminating condition was considered in calculation. From this result we have proposed this condition shall be included to the MIU.

articleTitle: Modelling of electrical percolation and conductivity of carbon nanotube based polymer nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Carbon nanotube based polymer nanocomposites due to their excellent electrical, thermal, mechanical and physical characteristics has emerged as a promising material in diverse fields like military, commercial, industrial sectors. The high electrical conductivity of carbon nanotubes is mainly responsible for such diverse applications as in aerospace and electromagnetic interference shielding. This paper deals with the modelling of electrical conductivity and percolation of carbon nanotube based composites for shielding application. It also deals with the effect of carbon nanotube dimensions and interface properties on electrical conductivity of the nanocomposite. It also explains the modification of the existing model so as to avoid the overestimation of electrical conductivity before percolation. The selection of optimum filler volume which helps in optimizing the cost involved in electromagnetic shield preparation is also discussed. Micromechanics modelling is used for estimating the electrical conductivity taking into account the electron hopping and the formation of conductive networks.

articleTitle: Impact on human exposure to low frequency radiation with psychological and brainwave changes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of exposure to low frequency (LF) radiation with psychological and brainwave changes. 22 subjects under a 100kHz and 0.5A/m magnetic exposure were investigated; the psychological status of the subjects was evaluated by Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS); their Electroencephalographs (EEGs) of the sham exposure and the control exposure were recorded. Outcomes of the experiment are correlated for the psychological changes and brainwave activity of human exposure. Statistical outcomes have indicated that the acute LF exposure will induce psychological changes but there were no significant brain wave changes. The significance level of the statistical outcomes of both psychological responses and the brain wave activity were confirmed with a pair t-test.

articleTitle: Non-ideal electric field shielding with grounding resistor for suppressing EMI coupling in a power converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: Shielding techniques are widely applied in suppression of near electric field interference from power converters, so as to enhance their electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) performance. However, sometimes traditional shielding method cannot effectively suppress the electromagnetic interference (EMI) in the full frequency range. In order to make a power converter meet the limit requirement of EMC standard, this paper proposes an improved non-ideal electric field shielding method to balance the suppression effects of the low frequency and high frequency interference. A resistor with appropriate resistance is connected between the shielding layer and the reference ground so as to balance the suppression effect of the high frequency and the low frequency interference. The EMI measurement results show that the power converter with improved shielding method had good EMC performance.

articleTitle: E-band multi-layer full-corporate-feed waveguide slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: A corporate feed waveguide slot array antenna with broad bandwidth characteristics is designed for the 73.5-GHz band (E-band) in order to increase the operating frequency band and the gain at the satellite communication frequency. The proposed antennas use multi layer feeding structure for stable fabrication process. An 8×8-elements array antenna shows 27.3dBi antenna gain with over 80% antenna efficiency and 7GHz bandwidth (69.9-76.9GHz), while 16×16-elements array antenna shows 33.8dBi antenna gain with over 80% antenna efficiency and more than 7GHz bandwidth (69.85-76.9GHz), and 32×32-elements array shows 39.9dBi antenna gain with over 70% antenna efficiency and more than 6.9GHz bandwidth (69.63-76.55GHz), respectively.

articleTitle: Application of the artificial material single layer (AMSL) method to assess the magnetic field generated by a WPT system with shield
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the recently developed artificial material single layer (AMSL) method is applied to model a conductive shield for wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. This method is very efficient in the simulation of a complex setup, such as that occurring in the analysis of the magnetic field produced by a WPT system installed in an electrical vehicle (EV). In this application, a critical issue is the efficient and accurate modeling of conductive shields to evaluate the near field magnetic field. To this aim, the AMSL method permits a significant reduction of the shield domain discretization and, therefore, of the computational time without altering the model physical geometry. A comparison of the AMSL with the traditional FEM solution is carried out showing very good results.

articleTitle: RFI suppression and throughput improvement of WiFi performance with graphene coating for converging mobile device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and 2018 IEEE Asia-Pacific Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC/APEMC)
abstract: As the wireless applications for high-performance computing and video streaming is booming, the converging high performance devices for wireless and mobile application bring up the platform noise and RFI de-sensitivity issue. The problem involving with electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) or radio frequency interference (RFI) is becoming more critical for the system integration of smart phones design. To prevent RFI noise coupling to sensitive RF front-end and thus degrading wireless communications performance, this paper is mainly focusing on the effective shielding analysis of graphene coating on RF noisy chips or modules. We first adopt the near-field electromagnetic interference (EMI) scanning methods developed by IEC for chip level (IEC 61967-3) to investigate the distribution of EMI noise sources characteristic on the smart-phone platform under investigation. To effectively shield the electric, magnetic, or electromagnetic field originated from noise source, we then apply the shielding capability of graphene coating on the RFI noisy sources. Finally, we will use Over-the-air (OTA) measurement to show the RF performance improvement with implementation of graphene coating from the relationship between data throughput increase and RFI reduction on chips or modules under investigation.
